FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/analyze/Analyzer.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompiledAdventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory

/**
 * Semantic analysis of an adventure that **compiles successfully**.
 *
 * **Scope.** The analyzer works on a
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompiledAdventure] — that is, after
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.Engine.compile] has built the indexes.
 * Anything that prevents compilation is
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompileError], not a [LintIssue]. Anything
 * that prevents **parsing** is
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseError]. The analyzer is the third
 * and last layer: "the file opens and plays, but is it coherent?" — same
 * boundary fixed in Ф1.3.4.1.
 *
 * **What the analyzer does not check (yet).**
 * - `nextScene` pointing to a scene that does not exist. It is checked
 *   implicitly by [reachable]: a `nextScene` to a missing scene is
 *   added to [reachable] (the id is recorded), but the scene is not in
 *   [CompiledAdventure.scenesById], so it is not further traversed. This
 *   is the same model as the current `:app` reader: it fails at the
 *   moment of transition, not at open time. A dedicated check
 *   ([LintKind.MissingNextScene]) will be added in Ф1.6.2 together with
 *   the `StoryValidator` port.
 * - `has_X` on numeric variable, unknown variable — type checker, Ф2.2.
 * - Duplicate `ChoiceId` within a scene — the reader looks choices up by
 *   id; a duplicate would be resolved to the first one. Will be a
 *   `LintKind.DuplicateChoiceId` in Ф1.6.2.
 *
 * **Determinism.** Both methods return values sorted by scene id, so
 * repeated runs on the same input produce identical output. This is a
 * prerequisite for snapshot tests of analyzer output in a later phase.
 */
public object Analyzer {

    /**
     * Builds a [ReachabilityReport] for [compiled].
     *
     * **BFS** from [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.startScene]
     * along `choice.nextScene` links. Every entry in
     * [ReachabilityReport.reachable] is guaranteed to exist in
     * [CompiledAdventure.scenesById] — so the UI can safely jump to any
     * scene id it finds there.
     *
     * **Missing references are not reachability.** A `nextScene` that
     * points to a scene not present in [CompiledAdventure.scenesById] is
     * **not** added to [ReachabilityReport.reachable] — "reachable" means
     * "the player can visit this scene", and a scene that does not exist
     * cannot be visited. The missing reference itself is a separate
     * problem ([LintKind.MissingNextScene], coming in Ф1.6.2), not a
     * reachability question.
     *
     * **Missing start scene.** If
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.startScene] itself is not
     * in [CompiledAdventure.scenesById] — a bug in the file, not caught
     * by `JsonToIr` because reference-integrity belongs to the analyzer —
     * [ReachabilityReport.reachable] is empty and every existing scene is
     * reported as unreachable. The missing start scene will surface as a
     * separate lint issue ([LintKind.MissingStartScene], Ф1.6.2).
     *
     * **Termination.** The BFS visits each scene at most once; `nextScene`
     * cycles (self-loops, `A → B → A`) are safe.
     */
    public fun reachable(compiled: CompiledAdventure): ReachabilityReport {
        val start = compiled.adventure.startScene
        val reachable = mutableSetOf<SceneId>()
        val queue = ArrayDeque<SceneId>()
        // Only seed the BFS if the start scene actually exists. If it does
        // not, `reachable` stays empty and every existing scene is reported
        // as unreachable — which is exactly the author's situation: nothing
        // can be visited. The missing start scene itself will be a lint
        // issue (`LintKind.MissingStartScene`, Ф1.6.2), not a reachability
        // answer.
        if (start in compiled.scenesById) {
            reachable.add(start)
            queue.addLast(start)
        }
        while (queue.isNotEmpty()) {
            val current = queue.removeFirst()
            val scene = compiled.scenesById[current] ?: continue
            for (choice in scene.choices) {
                // Only follow edges to scenes that actually exist. A
                // `nextScene` pointing to a missing scene is a separate
                // problem (missing-reference), not a reachability one; it
                // will be a lint issue in Ф1.6.2. Keeping missing ids out
                // of `reachable` means UI can safely jump to anything in
                // the set.
                if (choice.nextScene in compiled.scenesById &&
                    reachable.add(choice.nextScene)
                ) {
                    queue.addLast(choice.nextScene)
                }
            }
        }

        val allSceneIds = compiled.scenesById.keys
        val unreachable = (allSceneIds - reachable)
            .sortedBy { it.value }

        val deadEnds = reachable
            .filter { compiled.scenesById[it]?.choices?.isEmpty() == true }
            .sortedBy { it.value }

        return ReachabilityReport(
            reachable = reachable,
            unreachable = unreachable,
            deadEnds = deadEnds,
        )
    }

    /**
     * Returns all semantic issues found in [compiled].
     *
     * Today this is exactly [LintKind.UnreachableScene] for each scene in
     * [ReachabilityReport.unreachable]. Ф1.6.2 will add the existing
     * `StoryValidator` checks (dead ends without `isChapterEnd`, missing
     * `nextScene`, `set_flags` on `ITEM`/`HEALTH`, etc.) as additional
     * [LintKind] variants.
     *
     * **No false positives.** An empty list means the adventure is
     * semantically clean (by the current set of checks). The analyzer
     * never returns `WARNING`s for things the author cannot control.
     */
    public fun lint(compiled: CompiledAdventure): List<LintIssue> {
        val issues = mutableListOf<LintIssue>()
        issues += lintUnreachable(compiled)
        issues += lintRemovingUnestablishedItem(compiled)
        issues += lintDeathSceneWithoutHealth(compiled)
        issues += lintConditionOnUnestablishedFlag(compiled)
        issues += lintDeathWithoutDeathScene(compiled)
        issues += lintDeadEnd(compiled)
        issues += lintEndingSceneWithChoices(compiled)
        return issues.sortedWith(
            compareBy<LintIssue> { it.sceneId == null }
                .thenBy { it.sceneId?.value ?: "" }
                .thenBy { it.message },
        )
    }

    private fun lintUnreachable(compiled: CompiledAdventure): List<LintIssue> {
        val report = reachable(compiled)
        val startId = compiled.adventure.startScene.value
        return report.unreachable.map { sceneId ->
            LintIssue(
                kind = LintKind.UnreachableScene,
                message = "Scene '${sceneId.value}' is not reachable from " +
                        "start scene '$startId'",
                sceneId = sceneId,
                severity = Severity.WARNING,
            )
        }
    }

    private fun lintRemovingUnestablishedItem(compiled: CompiledAdventure): List<LintIssue> {
        val tags = compiled.adventure.tags.associateBy { it.name }
        val allScenes = compiled.adventure.chapters.flatMap { it.scenes }
        val allChoices = allScenes.flatMap { it.choices }

        // Establish what is "given": positive initial stats and positive
        // ModifyStat effects anywhere. If an ITEM/HEALTH variable is in
        // this set, reducing it is legitimate.
        val positiveSet = mutableSetOf<String>()
        compiled.adventure.initialState.stats.forEach { (name, value) ->
            if (value > 0) positiveSet.add(name)
        }
        for (effect in allScenes.flatMap { it.effects }) {
            if (effect is Effect.ModifyStat && effect.delta > 0) positiveSet.add(effect.name)
        }
        for (effect in allChoices.flatMap { it.effects }) {
            if (effect is Effect.ModifyStat && effect.delta > 0) positiveSet.add(effect.name)
        }

        fun isItemOrHealth(name: String): Boolean {
            val tag = tags[name] ?: return false
            return tag.category == TagCategory.ITEM || tag.category == TagCategory.HEALTH
        }

        val reported = mutableSetOf<Pair<SceneId, String>>()
        val issues = mutableListOf<LintIssue>()

        fun check(sceneId: SceneId, effect: Effect) {
            if (effect !is Effect.ModifyStat) return
            if (effect.delta >= 0) return
            if (!isItemOrHealth(effect.name)) return
            if (effect.name in positiveSet) return
            val key = sceneId to effect.name
            if (!reported.add(key)) return
            issues += LintIssue(
                kind = LintKind.RemovingUnestablishedItem(effect.name),
                message = "Scene '${sceneId.value}' reduces '${effect.name}' " +
                        "by ${-effect.delta}, but '${effect.name}' is never established " +
                        "(not in initial_state with a positive value, no positive change " +
                        "in any scene or choice). The player cannot use it.",
                sceneId = sceneId,
                severity = Severity.WARNING,
            )
        }

        for (scene in allScenes) {
            for (effect in scene.effects) check(scene.id, effect)
            for (choice in scene.choices) {
                for (effect in choice.effects) check(scene.id, effect)
            }
        }
        return issues
    }

    private fun lintDeathSceneWithoutHealth(compiled: CompiledAdventure): List<LintIssue> {
        if (compiled.adventure.deathScene == null) return emptyList()
        if (compiled.adventure.initialState.stats.containsKey("health")) return emptyList()
        val allScenes = compiled.adventure.chapters.flatMap { it.scenes }
        val hasHealthEffect = allScenes.any { scene ->
            scene.effects.any { it is Effect.ModifyStat && it.name == "health" } ||
                    scene.choices.any { choice ->
                        choice.effects.any { it is Effect.ModifyStat && it.name == "health" }
                    }
        }
        if (hasHealthEffect) return emptyList()
        return listOf(
            LintIssue(
                kind = LintKind.DeathSceneWithoutHealth,
                message = "Adventure has a death scene, but 'health' is never " +
                        "initialized (not in initial_state.stats) and never modified " +
                        "(no ModifyStat for 'health' in any scene or choice). " +
                        "Death will never occur.",
                sceneId = null,
                severity = Severity.WARNING,
            ),
        )
    }

    // ----- Ф1.6.2.3: condition on unestablished flag (port of :app check #4) -----

    private fun lintConditionOnUnestablishedFlag(
        compiled: CompiledAdventure,
    ): List<LintIssue> {
        // "Established" = the name appears somewhere the runtime can see it:
        //   - initial_state.flags (Bool flag set from the start)
        //   - initial_state.stats keys (numeric value set from the start;
        //     shim until Ф2.2, see LintKind.ConditionOnUnestablishedFlag KDoc)
        //   - any Effect.SetFlag in any scene or choice
        val establishable = mutableSetOf<String>()
        establishable += compiled.adventure.initialState.flags
        establishable += compiled.adventure.initialState.stats.keys
        val allScenes = compiled.adventure.chapters.flatMap { it.scenes }
        for (scene in allScenes) {
            for (effect in scene.effects) {
                if (effect is Effect.SetFlag) establishable.add(effect.name)
            }
            for (choice in scene.choices) {
                for (effect in choice.effects) {
                    if (effect is Effect.SetFlag) establishable.add(effect.name)
                }
            }
        }

        val issues = mutableListOf<LintIssue>()
        for (scene in allScenes) {
            for (choice in scene.choices) {
                val condition = choice.condition ?: continue
                val flags = collectHasFlags(condition)
                for (flag in flags.sorted()) {
                    if (flag in establishable) continue
                    issues += LintIssue(
                        kind = LintKind.ConditionOnUnestablishedFlag(flag),
                        message = "Choice '${choice.text}' in scene '${scene.id.value}' " +
                                "has condition referencing flag '$flag', but '$flag' never " +
                                "appears anywhere in the adventure (not in initial_state, " +
                                "no SetFlag effect in any scene or choice). The condition " +
                                "cannot behave as intended.",
                        sceneId = scene.id,
                        severity = Severity.WARNING,
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        return issues
    }

    /** Recursively collects every [Condition.Has] name (also inside Not/And/Or). */
    private fun collectHasFlags(condition: Condition): Set<String> {
        val result = mutableSetOf<String>()
        fun visit(c: Condition) {
            when (c) {
                is Condition.Has -> result.add(c.name)
                is Condition.Not -> visit(c.inner)
                is Condition.And -> { visit(c.left); visit(c.right) }
                is Condition.Or -> { visit(c.left); visit(c.right) }
                is Condition.Compare -> Unit // numeric, not a flag
                is Condition.InRange -> Unit // numeric, not a flag
            }
        }
        visit(condition)
        return result
    }

    // ----- Ф1.6.2.3: death without death scene (port of :app check #6) -----

    private fun lintDeathWithoutDeathScene(compiled: CompiledAdventure): List<LintIssue> {
        if (compiled.adventure.deathScene != null) return emptyList()
        val hasHealthInInitial = compiled.adventure.initialState.stats.containsKey("health")
        val hasHealthEffect = compiled.adventure.chapters.flatMap { it.scenes }.any { scene ->
            scene.effects.any { it is Effect.ModifyStat && it.name == "health" } ||
                    scene.choices.any { choice ->
                        choice.effects.any { it is Effect.ModifyStat && it.name == "health" }
                    }
        }
        if (!hasHealthInInitial && !hasHealthEffect) return emptyList()
        return listOf(
            LintIssue(
                kind = LintKind.DeathWithoutDeathScene,
                message = "Adventure uses 'health' but does not define a death_scene. " +
                        "When the player's health reaches 0, a default death screen will be " +
                        "shown. Add a death_scene to customize the message and the recovery " +
                        "options.",
                sceneId = null,
                severity = Severity.WARNING,
            ),
        )
    }

    // ----- Ф1.6.2.3: dead end (port of :app check #8, adapted to IR v3) -----

    private fun lintDeadEnd(compiled: CompiledAdventure): List<LintIssue> {
        val reachable = reachable(compiled).reachable
        val issues = mutableListOf<LintIssue>()
        for (chapter in compiled.adventure.chapters) {
            for (scene in chapter.scenes) {
                if (scene.choices.isNotEmpty()) continue
                if (scene.isEnding) continue // explicitly marked as an ending — ok
                if (scene.id !in reachable) continue // UnreachableScene covers this
                issues += LintIssue(
                    kind = LintKind.DeadEnd,
                    message = "Scene '${scene.id.value}' has no choices and is not marked " +
                            "as an ending. The player will see \"the end\" here and will not " +
                            "reach the remaining scenes. Either add choices or set " +
                            "\"is_ending\": true on this scene.",
                    sceneId = scene.id,
                    severity = Severity.WARNING,
                )
            }
        }
        return issues
    }

    // ----- Ф1.7.0: ending scene with choices -----

    private fun lintEndingSceneWithChoices(compiled: CompiledAdventure): List<LintIssue> {
        val issues = mutableListOf<LintIssue>()
        for (chapter in compiled.adventure.chapters) {
            for (scene in chapter.scenes) {
                if (!scene.isEnding) continue
                if (scene.choices.isEmpty()) continue
                issues += LintIssue(
                    kind = LintKind.EndingSceneWithChoices(scene.id),
                    message = "Scene '${scene.id.value}' is marked as an ending " +
                            "(\"is_ending\": true) but has ${scene.choices.size} choice(s). " +
                            "The reader shows the 'the end' screen and ignores the choices, " +
                            "so the player sees dead buttons. Either remove the choices or " +
                            "clear \"is_ending\".",
                    sceneId = scene.id,
                    severity = Severity.ERROR,
                )
            }
        }
        return issues
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/analyze/LintIssue.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId

/**
 * Severity of a [LintIssue].
 *
 * **Errors are not `LintIssue`s.** An error means "the file cannot be
 * opened or played" and lives in [com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseError]
 * or [com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompileError]. A [LintIssue] always means
 * "the file opens and plays, but something is wrong with it". This is the
 * parser/analyzer boundary fixed in Ф1.3.4.1.
 */
public enum class Severity {
    /**
     * The adventure runs, but something is almost certainly wrong
     * (unreachable scene, mistyped flag, dead code). The author should
     * fix it before shipping, but it will not break the player's
     * experience outright — the reader may simply reach content the
     * author did not intend.
     */
    WARNING,

    /**
     * The adventure is broken for the **player**, not just for the
     * author: a scene has no choices and no `is_ending` marker (the
     * player gets stuck on an empty screen with no way out), or a scene
     * is marked `is_ending` but also has choices (the reader shows a
     * "the end" screen with dead buttons).
     *
     * **[com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze.Analyzer] returns `ERROR`
     * only for issues that the reader must refuse to load** (Ф1.7.1 will
     * enforce this). Anything the player can still play through, even
     * if suboptimally, is `WARNING`, not `ERROR`. The author sees both
     * in the editor; only `ERROR` blocks opening the file from the
     * reader's library.
     */
    ERROR,

    /** Informational — e.g. "this scene has no choices, so the adventure ends here". */
    INFO,
}

/**
 * Type of a [LintIssue]. One variant per check.
 *
 * **Why sealed and not an enum.** Future checks need per-variant data
 * ([LintKind.UnreachableScene] today; `TypeMismatch(variable)` in Ф2.2,
 * `DeadCondition(condition)` in Ф3.6, `MergeConflict(nodeId)` in Ф4.6).
 * An enum cannot carry that data; a sealed class can grow without
 * breaking exhaustive `when` in the analyzer or in the UI.
 *
 * **Why the per-variant data does not also live in [LintIssue].** Each
 * variant knows its own context; the issue carries only the fields the
 * **UI** needs for navigation (message, scene id) — so that the UI can
 * `when` on `kind` when it wants, and fall back to generic rendering
 * otherwise. Adding a new variant means adding it to `LintKind` and
 * teaching the UI to render it; no changes to `LintIssue` itself.
 */
public sealed class LintKind {

    /**
     * A scene is not reachable from [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.startScene]
     * by following `choice.nextScene` links. The player can never see it.
     *
     * Almost always a mistake: a scene that was written but not wired up.
     * Occasionally intentional (a draft scene the author plans to link
     * later) — which is why this is a `WARNING`, not an error.
     */
    public data object UnreachableScene : LintKind()

    /**
     * A scene or choice reduces an `ITEM`/`HEALTH` variable that is never
     * established (not in `initialState.stats` with a positive value, and
     * not increased by any `ModifyStat` with `delta > 0`).
     *
     * The author probably forgot to grant the item before removing it.
     * The player will see a "−1 sword" effect and end up at 0 (clamped),
     * wondering where the sword came from.
     *
     * **WARNING, not ERROR.** It is possible for an author to write
     * `remove` without `grant` on purpose, e.g. "you drop the sword you
     * started with" where the sword was given in `initial_state.stats` —
     * but we already check `initial_state`, so the only way this fires is
     * when the item is genuinely never established. Still WARNING, because
     * the adventure still runs; it just looks wrong to the player.
     *
     * **Scope of "ITEM/HEALTH".** Today this is determined by
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagDefinition.category] in
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.tags]. If a variable is
     * used in an effect but not declared in `tags`, it is treated as
     * `JOURNAL` (the default) and this check does not fire. The type
     * checker (Ф2.2) is where "unknown variable" is caught.
     */
    public data class RemovingUnestablishedItem(
        public val variableName: String,
    ) : LintKind()

    /**
     * The adventure declares a death scene, but `health` is never
     * initialized or modified. The death scene is dead code: the player
     * can never die.
     *
     * **WARNING, not ERROR.** The adventure runs; it just silently never
     * reaches the death scene. The author may have intended a no-death
     * adventure, in which case they should remove the death scene
     * entirely — but that is their call, not the analyzer's.
     */
    public data object DeathSceneWithoutHealth : LintKind()

    /**
     * A choice's [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.Has] (including
     * inside [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.Not] /
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.And] /
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition.Or]) references a name
     * that **never appears in the adventure**:
     * - not in [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState.flags];
     * - not in [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState.stats]'s keys;
     * - not the target of any [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect.SetFlag]
     *   in any scene or choice.
     *
     * The author almost certainly mistyped the name (`has_swrod` for
     * `has_sword`), or removed the flag from wherever it used to be set
     * and forgot to update the condition.
     *
     * **Shim note (Ф1.6).** For now this check treats *stats keys* as
     * "established" as well, because the current `test_adventure.json`
     * uses `has_sword` while `sword` is declared as `ItemCount`. A
     * strict reading ("`has_X` is only valid when `X` is a boolean
     * flag") belongs to the type checker, which lands in Ф2.2 as
     * `HasOnNonBoolVariable`. The intention of this check is narrower:
     * catch names that **do not exist anywhere**. Type mismatch
     * (`has_sword` on `sword: ItemCount`) is a different, orthogonal
     * problem and stays deferred.
     *
     * **WARNING, not ERROR.** The adventure opens and plays. The
     * condition on this choice, though, will never behave as intended:
     * `has_X` will evaluate to `false` at runtime, so the choice will
     * be silently disabled. Once Ф2.2 exists, this will be raised
     * earlier as a compile-time error (unknown variable), but the
     * transition period still benefits from the warning.
     *
     * @property flagName the name as it appears in the AST.
     */
    public data class ConditionOnUnestablishedFlag(
        public val flagName: String,
    ) : LintKind()

    /**
     * The adventure uses `health` (declared in
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState.stats] or modified by a
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect.ModifyStat] with
     * `name == "health"` in any scene or choice), but does **not**
     * define [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.deathScene].
     *
     * The player's health can reach 0 and the reader will fall back to a
     * built-in default death screen — which the author probably did not
     * intend. Inverse of [DeathSceneWithoutHealth]: that one fires when
     * the death screen exists but can never be reached; this one fires
     * when the death screen is reachable but does not exist.
     *
     * **WARNING, not ERROR.** The adventure runs and ends; the default
     * death screen is a reasonable fallback. The author just gets a
     * generic message instead of their authored one.
     */
    public data object DeathWithoutDeathScene : LintKind()

    /**
     * A reachable scene has no [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene.choices]
     * and is **not** marked
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene.isEnding] = `true`. The player
     * will see "the end" here and will not reach the remaining scenes.
     *
     * Since Ф1.7.0, "no choices" alone is no longer an implicit ending —
     * an ending **must** be explicit via `is_ending`. This is a project
     * decision (2026-11-07): pre-alpha drops backward compatibility, and
     * the reader no longer guesses "no choices = advance to the next
     * chapter". The rule is: a scene is either (a) non-terminal (has
     * choices), or (b) explicitly marked as an ending
     * (`is_ending = true`, no choices).
     *
     * **WARNING, not ERROR (revised 2026-11-07).** The player gets
     * warned, but **is not blocked** from opening the file: the reader
     * shows a "N warnings — continue?" dialog and lets the player
     * decide. An unfinished story (author forgot to mark the ending,
     * or intentionally left it open) is a *quality* problem, not a
     * *usability* blocker — the player can still read the whole story
     * up to that point. The original decision (2026-11-07, morning)
     * made this an `ERROR` on the reasoning "player gets stuck on a
     * blank screen"; the user pointed out that a blank screen the
     * player chose to reach is not the same as a screen with dead
     * buttons, and the reader should not override the player's
     * decision to keep reading. Only genuinely broken constructs
     * ([EndingSceneWithChoices] — the player would see buttons that
     * do nothing when clicked) remain `ERROR`.
     *
     * **Why not silently pass.** The warning dialog names the scene,
     * so a player who reaches the dead end and decides to report it
     * has a concrete pointer to send the author.
     *
     * **Not the same as [UnreachableScene].** An unreachable terminal
     * scene (no choices, no `is_ending`, and cannot be reached from
     * `start_scene`) is reported as [UnreachableScene], not as this:
     * the player never sees it, so there is nothing to unstick.
     */
    public data object DeadEnd : LintKind()

    /**
     * A scene is marked
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene.isEnding] = `true` **and** has
     * one or more [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene.choices].
     *
     * The reader (Ф1.7.1) will show the "the end" screen and ignore the
     * choices — the player sees dead buttons that do nothing. The author
     * almost certainly either (a) forgot to remove the choices, or (b)
     * accidentally ticked "end of game" on a non-terminal scene.
     *
     * **ERROR, not WARNING.** Unlike `WARNING`-level issues ("the
     * adventure runs, author should fix"), this is a contradiction the
     * author must resolve before the file makes sense. The reader refuses
     * to load it (Ф1.7.1).
     *
     * @property sceneId the contradictory scene.
     */
    public data class EndingSceneWithChoices(
        public val sceneId: SceneId,
    ) : LintKind()
}

/**
 * One semantic problem found by [Analyzer].
 *
 * **Rendering.** [message] is a fully-formed English string ready to show
 * to the author. It already mentions the scene by name/id, so the UI does
 * not need to reconstruct it. [sceneId] is the navigation hook: clicking
 * the issue in the editor (Ф9.2) jumps to this scene. `null` for issues
 * that do not belong to a specific scene (none today; future checks such
 * as "adventure has no chapters" might).
 *
 * **Ordering.** The analyzer returns issues sorted by scene id, so that
 * repeated runs produce identical output (important for golden tests of
 * the analyzer output later, and for stable UI).
 */
public data class LintIssue(
    public val kind: LintKind,
    public val message: String,
    public val sceneId: SceneId? = null,
    public val severity: Severity = Severity.WARNING,
)

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/analyze/ReachabilityReport.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId

/**
 * Result of [Analyzer.reachable].
 *
 * Three disjoint (well, almost — see below) sets, each answering a
 * different author question:
 *
 * - **[reachable]** — "which scenes can the player actually visit?" This
 *   is the graph reachable from
 *   [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.startScene] via
 *   `choice.nextScene` links.
 * - **[unreachable]** — "which scenes are written but never seen?" The
 *   author almost certainly forgot to wire them up. Empty is good.
 * - **[deadEnds]** — "which scenes end the adventure?" Scenes reachable
 *   from the start with no `choices`. **These are not problems** — an
 *   adventure has to end somewhere — but the author wants a list, because
 *   an *unintended* dead end (a scene they thought had choices) is a bug.
 *
 * **Overlap.** [reachable] and [deadEnds] are **not** disjoint: every dead
 * end is reachable (by definition — an unreachable dead end is just
 * unreachable, and we do not list it twice). [unreachable] is disjoint
 * from the other two by construction.
 *
 * **Missing start scene.** If
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.startScene] is not in
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompiledAdventure.scenesById] (a bug in
 * the file, not caught by `JsonToIr` because the analyzer is where
 * reference-integrity lives — see Ф1.6.2), every scene is reported as
 * [unreachable] and [reachable] is empty. The analyzer does **not**
 * throw; a bug is a bug, and the reader will show an error screen if the
 * player opens the file anyway.
 *
 * @property reachable scenes the player can visit from the start scene.
 * @property unreachable scenes not reachable from the start scene, sorted
 *   by id for stable output.
 * @property deadEnds reachable scenes with no choices, sorted by id.
 */
public data class ReachabilityReport(
    public val reachable: Set<SceneId>,
    public val unreachable: List<SceneId>,
    public val deadEnds: List<SceneId>,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Root of the IR: a complete adventure.
 *
 * Produced by the JSON parser (Ф1.3), consumed by the runtime (Ф1.5), the
 * analyzer (Ф1.6), and the exporter (Ф8). There is exactly one `Adventure`
 * per file; there are no cross-adventure references.
 *
 * **Not the same as `:app/data/Adventure.kt`.** The IR is typed
 * (see [Condition], [Effect], [VarType], [SceneId]), non-null where
 * sensible, and carries a [version] for migration. The Android Gson-POJO
 * remains as the on-disk DTO for the editor; the adapter (Ф1.7) converts
 * between the two.
 *
 * @property version IR schema version. The parser (Ф1.3) reads it from the
 *   file; if absent, assumes [CURRENT_VERSION]. Migrations live alongside
 *   the parser and are applied on load (Ф5.3). Bumping this is a breaking
 *   change to the on-disk format and requires a migration entry.
 * @property title adventure title; shown in the library and reader.
 * @property author author name; informational.
 * @property description short blurb; shown in the library.
 * @property variables registry of variables used by [Condition] and
 *   [Effect]. Empty means "no declared variables" — such an adventure
 *   type-checks only against [InitialState] (Ф2 migration will populate
 *   this for existing files; new files are expected to declare variables
 *   explicitly).
 * @property tags registry of tags with display metadata; used by the
 *   reader's HUD to decide what to show and how.
 * @property initialState player state before the first scene.
 * @property deathScene optional death screen; `null` means the runtime
 *   uses built-in defaults.
 * @property startScene scene the player begins in. Explicit since IR v3;
 *   in v1/v2 files the field was absent and the parser inferred it from
 *   `chapters.first().scenes.first()`. Making it explicit lets authors
 *   start in a scene that is not the first in the first chapter (for
 *   example: a dramatic teaser, then a prologue via `nextScene`). The
 *   analyzer's reachability (Ф1.6.1) uses this as the root of the graph.
 * @property chapters ordered list of chapters. Must be non-empty; enforced
 *   by the parser (Ф1.3).
 */
@Serializable
public data class Adventure(
    public val version: Int = CURRENT_VERSION,
    public val title: String,
    public val author: String = "",
    public val description: String = "",
    public val variables: Map<String, VarDecl> = emptyMap(),
    public val tags: List<TagDefinition> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("initial_state")
    public val initialState: InitialState = InitialState(),
    @SerialName("death_scene")
    public val deathScene: DeathScene? = null,
    @SerialName("start_scene")
    public val startScene: SceneId,
    public val chapters: List<Chapter>,
){
    public companion object {
        /**
         * Current IR schema version. Increment when the on-disk format
         * changes in a way that old files cannot be read as-is; add a
         * migration in the parser at the same time.
         *
         * Version history:
         * - `1` — initial IR (Ф1.2): typed `Condition`/`Effect`,
         *   `SceneId` value class, `variables` registry, `version` field.
         *   Files that predate IR have no `version`; they are treated as
         *   `1` and migrated by the parser if needed. Gates lived on
         *   chapters as `chapter.required_steps`.
         * - `2` (Ф1.5.4) — gates moved from chapters to scenes.
         *   `Chapter.required_steps` is removed; `Scene.gate: Gate?`
         *   is added. Migration in `JsonToIr`: `chapter[i].required_steps
         *   = N > 0` becomes `Gate(N)` on the last scene of chapter `i-1`.
         *   Files without `version` are migrated from v1.
         * - `3` (Ф1.6.0) — `Adventure.start_scene: SceneId` added.
         *   Before v3, the start scene was inferred from
         *   `chapters.first().scenes.first()`; the analyzer's reachability
         *   (Ф1.6.1) needs an explicit root, because an author may start
         *   in a scene that is not the first in the first chapter.
         *   Migration in `JsonToIr`: `start_scene` absent → inferred from
         *   `chapters.first().scenes.first()` (identity for all existing
         *   files). Files without `version` are migrated from v1.
         * - `4` (Ф1.7.0) — `Scene.is_ending: Boolean` added. The reader
         *   no longer guesses "no choices = end of chapter, auto-advance";
         *   an ending **must** be explicit. Multiple scenes may be marked
         *   `is_ending = true` (multiple endings). Migration v3 → v4:
         *   identity — v3 files have no `is_ending`, so the field defaults
         *   to `false`. Old files that relied on "no choices = end" now
         *   produce `DeadEnd` ERROR (per project decision 2026-11-07:
         *   pre-alpha drops backward compatibility, authors fix files).
         *   `test_adventure.json` is updated in the same release to mark
         *   its `final` scene as `is_ending = true`.
         * - `5` (Ф1.7.0.4) — `Gate.repeatable: Boolean` added. Default
         *   `false` ("once walked, stays open in this playthrough"),
         *   matching the common case "walk N steps to unlock the next
         *   chapter". `true` = per-visit ("travelled a path; the same
         *   path back costs the same steps"). The author picks the
         *   mode in the editor. `Gate` changed from `value class` to
         *   `data class`; IR serialization wraps the gate as
         *   `{"required_steps": N, "repeatable": bool}`. Adventure file
         *   format stays flat: `"gate": N` + optional
         *   `"gate_repeatable": true`. Migration v4 → v5: identity —
         *   v4 files have no `gate_repeatable`, so `repeatable = false`.
         */
        public const val CURRENT_VERSION: Int = 5
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/Chapter.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * A group of [Scene]s — **pure narrative grouping**.
 *
 * A chapter has no mechanical meaning of its own: it does not gate
 * anything, it does not impose a step requirement, it does not block
 * transitions. Its only jobs are:
 * 1. A human-readable [title] for the reader's chapter HUD and for the
 *    editor's map view.
 * 2. A stable [id] for logging and for `Analyzer` reports.
 * 3. Grouping scenes into a list for the UI.
 *
 * **Where gates live now.** Step gates moved from chapters to **scenes**
 * in Ф1.5.4: see [Scene.gate] and [Gate]. This means:
 * - A chapter may have zero, one, or several gated scenes.
 * - A gate may sit anywhere in a chapter (first, middle, last scene).
 * - A choice may lead to a scene in **another chapter** — chapters are
 *   not barriers.
 * - An adventure may have no gates at all: chapters are then just titles
 *   over a flat list of scenes.
 *
 * **Why the old `requiredSteps` field was removed.** It conflated two
 * unrelated concepts ("this is a boundary between narrative groups" and
 * "the player must walk N steps to proceed"). Authors asked for gates
 * in the middle of a chapter, or for chapter boundaries without gates,
 * or for multiple gates within one chapter — all impossible with the
 * old model. See the Progress log entry for Ф1.5.4 for the analysis.
 *
 * **Migration from v1 files** (which used `chapter.required_steps`):
 * `JsonToIr` moves `chapter[i].required_steps = N > 0` onto the **last
 * scene of chapter `i-1`** as `Gate(N)` — the same mechanical effect,
 * expressed on the scene that the player must leave to enter chapter
 * `i`. The first chapter's `required_steps` is dropped (it was always 0).
 *
 * **Chapters are ordered.** The order in [Adventure.chapters] determines
 * the reading sequence and the grouping in the UI. There is no explicit
 * "next chapter" reference; a scene transition to the first scene of a
 * later chapter is expressed via [Choice.nextScene].
 *
 * @property id stable chapter identifier (e.g. `"chapter_1"`).
 * @property title human-readable chapter title.
 * @property scenes scenes that belong to this chapter, in reading order.
 *   Must be non-empty; enforced by the parser (Ф1.3).
 */
@Serializable
public data class Chapter(
    public val id: String,
    public val title: String,
    public val scenes: List<Scene>,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * A single selectable action in a [Scene].
 *
 * Corresponds to `:app/data/Adventure.kt`'s `Choice`:
 * `text`, `next_scene`, `condition`, and the three effect fields
 * (`set_flags`, `remove_flags`, `modify_stats`) flattened into [effects].
 *
 * **Order matters.** When the player picks a choice, [effects] are applied
 * in list order (Ф1.5), matching the current reader behaviour where
 * `set_flags` run before `modify_stats`.
 *
 * **Availability.** A `null` [condition] means "always available". A
 * non-null [condition] is evaluated by the engine (Ф3); today's reader
 * (`AdventureReaderFragment.updateChoices`) hides unavailable choices.
 * The planned N4 / Ф4 behaviour is to show them as disabled with a
 * reason — that is a UI decision and does not affect this data model.
 *

 * @property nextScene scene the player transitions to when picking this
 *   choice. Required — there is no "do nothing" choice; use a self-loop
 *   (`nextScene = currentScene.id`) if you want the player to stay.
 * @property condition optional gate; `null` means always available.
 * @property effects state changes applied on pick, in order.
 */
@Serializable
public data class Choice(
    public val id: ChoiceId,
    public val text: String,
    @SerialName("next_scene")
    public val nextScene: SceneId,
    public val condition: Condition? = null,
    public val effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlin.jvm.JvmInline

/**
 * Stable identifier of a [Choice] within a scene.
 *
 * Wraps a [String] so that a choice reference cannot be confused with a
 * scene id ([SceneId]), a flag name, a stat name, or any other plain
 * string. Zero runtime cost — `@JvmInline value class` is erased to the
 * underlying `String` on JVM.
 *
 * **Serialized transparently** as the underlying string (same as
 * [SceneId]): `ChoiceId("c1")` appears in JSON as `"c1"`, not as
 * `{"value":"c1"}`.
 *
 * **Why a separate id at all.** Before Ф1.5 a choice had no id: the reader
 * identified it by index in `scene.choices`. That is fragile: inserting a
 * choice in the editor shifts every later index, and an old save that
 * referenced "the 3rd choice" now points at a different choice. The player
 * returns next day, presses "continue", and lands somewhere they never
 * picked. A stable [ChoiceId] makes saves survive edits.
 *
 * **Uniqueness** is enforced by the analyzer (Ф1.6), not by the type:
 * two `ChoiceId("c1")` are the same value. Duplicate detection within a
 * scene is an analyzer concern.
 *
 * **Generation.** When the JSON does not carry `id` for a choice,
 * `JsonToIr` generates `"<scene_id>_choice_<index>"` — deterministic and
 * stable for a given scene layout. Adding an explicit `id` in JSON
 * overrides the generated one.
 */
@Serializable
@JvmInline
public value class ChoiceId(public val value: String)

 * they match the operator symbols (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `!=`).

@Serializable
public enum class CompareOp {
    @SerialName("lt")
    LT,

    @SerialName("le")
    LE,

    @SerialName("gt")
    GT,

    @SerialName("ge")
    GE,

    @SerialName("eq")
    EQ,

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/Condition.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * AST of a condition that gates a choice, a scene, or an invariant.
 *
 * In `:app/data/Adventure.kt` conditions are plain strings
 * (`"has_sword"`, `"health >= 50"`). In the IR they are a typed tree:
 * the string is parsed once in `JsonToIr` (Ф1.3), and every consumer
 * (`evaluator` in Ф3, `Analyzer` in Ф1.6, future JS runtime in E1)
 * works with this tree instead of re-parsing strings.
 *
 * **Not included yet** (deferred to Ф3.2 / N7.base): `VarRef` as a
 * standalone node for arithmetic like `health + stamina > 50`. Add it
 * as a new subclass when needed — existing subclasses do not change.
 */
@Serializable
public sealed class Condition {

    /**
     * `has_X` — true if boolean flag `X` is set.
     *
     * **Only for [VarType.Bool] variables.** For numeric variables
     * ([VarType.Integer], [VarType.IntRange], [VarType.ItemCount]) use
     * [Compare] instead: `sword > 0` rather than `has_sword`,
     * `health > 0` rather than `has_health`. The type checker (Ф2.2)
     * rejects `Has` on non-boolean variables with a hint to use [Compare].
     *
     * The parser (Ф1.3) does **not** enforce this — it is a pure
     * syntactic transformation `"has_X"` → `Has("X")` and knows nothing
     * about variable types. Type checking is the single responsibility of
     * Ф2.2, which keeps parser and type checker decoupled.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("has")
    public data class Has(
        public val name: String,
    ) : Condition()

    /** `!X` — logical negation of [inner]. */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("not")
    public data class Not(
        public val inner: Condition,
    ) : Condition()

    /** `X && Y` — logical conjunction. Short-circuits left to right. */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("and")
    public data class And(
        public val left: Condition,
        public val right: Condition,
    ) : Condition()

    /** `X || Y` — logical disjunction. Short-circuits left to right. */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("or")
    public data class Or(
        public val left: Condition,
        public val right: Condition,
    ) : Condition()

    /**
     * `X <op> N` — comparison of variable [varName] against integer [value].
     *
     * `varName` must resolve to [VarType.Integer] or [VarType.IntRange];
     * anything else is a type error (Ф2). [CompareOp] determines the operator.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("compare")
    public data class Compare(
        @SerialName("var_name")
        public val varName: String,
        public val op: CompareOp,
        public val value: Int,
    ) : Condition()

    /**
     * `X in min..max` — inclusive range check for variable [varName].
     *
     * `varName` must resolve to [VarType.IntRange] (or [VarType.Integer]
     * when `min..max` is inside `IntRange` bounds); checked in Ф2.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("in_range")
    public data class InRange(
        @SerialName("var_name")
        public val varName: String,
        public val min: Int,
        public val max: Int,
    ) : Condition()
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Describes how the player dies and what recovery options they get.
 *
 * Corresponds to `:app/data/Adventure.kt`'s `DeathScene`.
 *
 * **Not a real [Scene].** The death screen is not part of the chapter
 * sequence: it is shown when the player's `health` reaches zero (or another
 * death invariant fires — see Ф3.5). Modelling it as a separate class keeps
 * [Chapter.scenes] clean of pseudo-scenes that would confuse the analyzer
 * (reachability, chapter grouping).
 *
 * **Default id.** If the adventure file omits `death_scene.id`, the parser
 * (Ф1.3) uses `"death_scene"`, matching
 * `AdventureEditorViewModel.buildAdventure()`.
 *
 * **All three `allow*` flags default to `true`.** The current
 * `DeathScene` in `:app` has the same defaults; matching them keeps
 * `test_adventure.json` (which sets them explicitly) and adventures that
 * omit them behave identically.
 *
 * @property id scene-like identifier used by the reader for logging and
 *   for the "step back" mechanism.
 * @property text death message shown to the player.
 * @property allowStepBack whether the "step back" recovery button is shown.
 * @property allowChapterRestart whether the "restart chapter" button is shown.
 * @property allowAdventureRestart whether the "restart adventure" button is shown.
 */
@Serializable
public data class DeathScene(
    public val id: SceneId = SceneId("death_scene"),
    public val text: String = "💀 Вы погибли.",
    @SerialName("allow_step_back")
    public val allowStepBack: Boolean = true,
    @SerialName("allow_chapter_restart")
    public val allowChapterRestart: Boolean = true,
    @SerialName("allow_adventure_restart")
    public val allowAdventureRestart: Boolean = true,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * A single state-modifying effect attached to a [Scene] or [Choice].
 *
 * In `:app/data/Adventure.kt` effects are three parallel nullable fields
 * (`set_flags`, `remove_flags`, `modify_stats`). In the IR each individual
 * change is one [Effect], and the parser (Ф1.3) turns the three fields into
 * a flat `List<Effect>`. Runtime applies effects in declaration order
 * (Ф1.5), so reordering affects semantics — that is intentional and
 * matches the current reader behaviour.
 *
 * Effects are **applied once** when a scene is first entered or when a
 * choice is picked. See `AdventureReaderFragment.applyEffects` for the
 * reference semantics.
 */
@Serializable
public sealed class Effect {

    /**
     * `set_flags` entry: add [name] to the player's flag set (if not
     * already present). Idempotent.
     *
     * Only meaningful for [TagCategory.JOURNAL] tags; the type checker (Ф2)
     * will reject `set_flags` on `ITEM`/`HEALTH` tags.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("set_flag")
    public data class SetFlag(
        public val name: String,
    ) : Effect()

    /**
     * `remove_flags` entry: remove [name] from the player's flag set
     * (if present). Idempotent.
     *
     * Only meaningful for [TagCategory.JOURNAL] tags; `ITEM`/`HEALTH`
     * tags are removed by setting their value to zero via [ModifyStat].
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("remove_flag")
    public data class RemoveFlag(
        public val name: String,
    ) : Effect()

    /**
     * `modify_stats` entry: add [delta] to the current value of [name].
     *
     * **Delta semantics, not absolute.** If the current value is `10` and
     * `delta` is `-3`, the new value is `7`. This matches the current
     * `AdventureReaderFragment.applyEffects`.
     *
     * For [TagCategory.HEALTH] and [TagCategory.ITEM] variables the result
     * is clamped to `>= 0` (current behaviour). For [TagCategory.JOURNAL]
     * numeric values there is no clamping. Clamping policy lives in the
     * runtime (Ф1.5), not here — [Effect] is a pure data description.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("modify_stat")
    public data class ModifyStat(
        public val name: String,
        public val delta: Int,
    ) : Effect()
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/Gate.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * A step gate on a [Scene]: the player must walk at least [requiredSteps]
 * real-world steps after entering this scene before any exit is allowed
 * (picking a choice, or auto-advancing to the next scene/chapter).
 *
 * **Where gates live.** A gate belongs to the **scene it gates the exit
 * of**, not to the chapter it opens. A chapter is pure narrative
 * grouping; a gate is a mechanical requirement on a single scene. A gate
 * may sit anywhere in a chapter, several gates may sit in one chapter,
 * and a chapter may have none.
 *
 * **Two modes** ([repeatable]):
 *
 * - **`repeatable = false` (default).** "Once walked, always open **in
 *   this playthrough**". The gate blocks the first time the player
 *   enters the scene; after [requiredSteps] are accumulated, the gate is
 *   marked as passed for this playthrough and **does not re-engage** if
 *   the player returns to this scene. Resetting the adventure
 *   (`restart`) clears the pass. Use this for the common case: "walk
 *   N steps to unlock the next chapter" — once unlocked, the player
 *   never re-walks.
 * - **`repeatable = true`.** Per-visit. Each time the player enters
 *   this scene (including by picking a choice that self-loops back to
 *   it), they must walk [requiredSteps] again. Use this for the
 *   "travelled a path" case: the player physically walks from location
 *   A to location B; returning to A and travelling to B again requires
 *   the same walk. Also useful for time-gated scenes: "you must wait
 *   N steps before you can pick anything here" — every visit.
 *
 * The author picks the mode in the editor. Default is `false` because
 * the "re-walked" surprise is worse than "unlocked but stays unlocked":
 * a player who unlocked a chapter once does not expect to unlock it
 * again by accident.
 *
 * **In JSON (adventure file format)** the gate is a flat pair:
 * `"gate": 4000` (required steps) and, optionally,
 * `"gate_repeatable": true`. `gate_repeatable` defaults to `false`, so
 * simple gates stay one-key.
 *
 * **In the IR** `Gate` is a data class with two fields
 * ([requiredSteps] and [repeatable]). The reason it is not a
 * `value class` anymore: `value class` requires exactly one field, and
 * we need two. IR serialization therefore wraps the gate as
 * `{"required_steps": N, "repeatable": bool}`. This is **IR
 * serialization**, not adventure file format — the two are different
 * by design (`golden_ir.json` is IR, not adventure).
 *
 * **Positive by construction.** `requiredSteps <= 0` is meaningless
 * ("walk at least 0 steps" = "no gate"). The parser (`JsonToIr`)
 * rejects `gate <= 0` as a structural error; `Gate(0)` should never be
 * constructed. "No gate" is `Scene.gate == null`.
 *
 * **Not checked by `Engine.step`.** Step counting is a reader concern
 * (a foreground service in `:app`). The engine does not know how many
 * steps the player has walked, nor whether a gate was already passed;
 * it only knows the mechanical shape of the gate. The reader checks the
 * gate, tracks which gates have been passed (per playthrough for
 * `repeatable = false`, per-visit for `repeatable = true`), and only
 * calls `Engine.step` when the current gate is open. This keeps the
 * engine free of wall-clock and sensor dependencies.
 *
 * @property requiredSteps number of steps to accumulate before the
 *   scene becomes exitable. Must be strictly positive.
 * @property repeatable whether the gate re-engages on every visit
 *   (`true`) or once passed stays passed for this playthrough
 *   (`false`, default).
 */
@Serializable
public data class Gate(
    @SerialName("required_steps")
    public val requiredSteps: Int,
    public val repeatable: Boolean = false,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Player state at the very start of an adventure, before the first scene
 * is entered.
 *
 * Corresponds to `:app/data/Adventure.kt`'s `PlayerState`, with one
 * difference: [flags] and [stats] are non-null with empty defaults, not
 * nullable. Nullable collections force every consumer to write
 * `?: emptyList()` at each call site; the IR instead says "no flags" as
 * `emptyList()`. The parser (Ф1.3) maps JSON's absent `null` / missing
 * fields to those defaults.
 *
 * **Precedence against [VarDecl]:** if a variable is declared in
 * [Adventure.variables] but not listed in [flags] / [stats], its value is
 * the type's default (see [VarType] KDoc). If listed, the value here wins.
 * This is the same as the current reader's `initNormalState()` behaviour.
 *
 * **Type consistency:** every flag / stat name here must be declared in
 * [Adventure.variables] — enforced by the type checker in Ф2.
 *
 * @property flags flags the player starts with.
 * @property stats numeric values the player starts with.
 */
@Serializable
public data class InitialState(
    public val flags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    public val stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
)

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/ir/PlayerState.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

/**
 * Player state during an adventure: what the player has right now.
 *
 * **Immutable.** Every change produces a new instance via [copy]. This
 * makes three things trivial that would otherwise be error-prone:
 *
 * 1. **Undo / "step back" after death.** Snapshot the state before the
 *    step; restoring it is `state = savedState`, no deep copy, no
 *    rollback logic. Already used by the reader
 *    (`previousStepSnapshot`, `chapterStartSnapshot`).
 * 2. **Save / load.** A state is a value; serializing it (Ф5/S5) is
 *    straightforward. Snapshots can be compared with `==`.
 * 3. **Unit testing.** `applyEffects(state, effects)` returns a new state;
 *    no shared mutable state between tests, no setup/teardown.
 *
 * The cost — one allocation per change — is negligible in the reader:
 * at most one change per user tap. The editor does not use
 * [PlayerState] at all (it works with `EditorModels`).
 *
 * **Distinct from [InitialState].**
 * - [InitialState] is part of the adventure data: "with what flags/stats
 *   does the player start". Serialized in JSON.
 * - [PlayerState] is runtime state: "where the player is now". Never
 *   serialized as part of [Adventure]; persists via the separate progress
 *   file (Ф5/S5).
 *
 * The reader creates a `PlayerState` from an `InitialState` at adventure
 * start; the analyzer (Ф1.6) uses both to reason about reachable states.
 *
 * **Flags vs stats.**
 * - [flags] — boolean markers ("visited_forest", "knows_secret").
 * - [stats] — numeric values ("health" = 100, "gold" = 5).
 *
 * Which side a variable lives on is determined by its declared type
 * ([VarType.Bool] → [flags]; anything numeric → [stats]). If the same
 * name appears in both, the analyzer reports it — either the author has
 * a genuine naming collision or the type checker (Ф2) will catch it.
 *
 * **No clamping here.** This class is a pure value: it does not enforce
 * that "health" stays non-negative. That policy lives in `Engine.applyEffects`
 * (Ф1.5), because clamping depends on the variable's declared type
 * (`HEALTH`/`ITEM` → `>= 0` after Ф2.8; unbounded for `Integer`). Keeping
 * the policy out of the data type keeps [PlayerState] reusable across
 * reader, analyzer, and any future UI preview.
 *
 * @property flags boolean flags currently true.
 * @property stats numeric values currently held.
 */
public data class PlayerState(
    public val flags: Set<String> = emptySet(),
    public val stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
)

/**
 * Creates a [PlayerState] from the adventure's [InitialState].
 *
 * The reader calls this once at adventure start (and on "restart
 * adventure") to build the first [PlayerState] from the JSON-declared
 * starting flags/stats. The engine does not depend on this function:
 * `Engine.step` always takes a [PlayerState], never an [InitialState].
 *
 * Collections are copied (`toSet`/`toMap`) so the [PlayerState] does not
 * alias the [InitialState] lists. Immutability is the whole point of
 * [PlayerState]; sharing a mutable backing would break that invariant.
 */
public fun InitialState.toPlayerState(): PlayerState =
    PlayerState(flags = flags.toSet(), stats = stats.toMap())

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * One screen of an adventure: body text, optional effects, and (optionally)
 * a list of [Choice]s the player can pick.
 *
 * Corresponds to `:app/data/Adventure.kt`'s `Scene`, with two differences:
 *
 * 1. The three JSON fields `set_flags`, `remove_flags`, `modify_stats` are
 *    flattened into [effects] (see [Effect]). Order is preserved by the
 *    parser (Ф1.3): `set_flags` first, then `remove_flags`, then
 *    `modify_stats`, matching the current reader's `applyEffects`.
 * 2. Scenes are grouped into [Chapter]s. There is no `isChapterEnd` flag in
 *    the IR: chapter boundaries are the boundaries of [Chapter.scenes].
 *
 * **A scene with no [choices]** is a terminal scene: the story **must**
 * mark it with [isEnding] = `true`, or the analyzer reports
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze.LintKind.DeadEnd] (severity
 * `ERROR`). The reader does **not** guess: it never auto-advances to the
 * next chapter. "End of chapter" must be expressed by an explicit
 * Continue-choice that leads to the first scene of the next chapter.
 *
 * @property id unique scene identifier within an adventure.
 * @property text body text shown to the player.
 * @property effects state changes applied the first time the scene is
 *   entered, in order. Re-entering a scene does not re-apply them.
 * @property choices actions shown below the text; may be empty.
 * @property gate optional step gate: the player must walk
 *   [Gate.requiredSteps] steps **after entering this scene** before any
 *   exit is allowed. `null` means "no gate". Gates are independent of
 *   chapters — a chapter may have zero, one, or many gated scenes, and a
 *   gated scene may sit anywhere in a chapter. See [Gate] for details.
 * @property isEnding whether this scene ends the adventure. Multiple
 *   scenes in the same adventure may be marked `true` — that is how
 *   authors model multiple endings ("win" / "die" / "retire rich" /
 *   etc.). A scene marked `true` **must** have no [choices] — the reader
 *   would otherwise render buttons that lead nowhere. Marking a scene
 *   with [isEnding] = `true` **and** non-empty [choices] is reported by
 *   [com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze.LintKind.EndingSceneWithChoices]
 *   (severity `ERROR`). Defaults to `false`; this matches the
 *   pre-`isEnding` behaviour, where "no choices" silently meant "end".
 *
 * **Not to be confused with [DeathScene].** `DeathScene` is not part of
 * [Chapter.scenes] and does not carry [isEnding]. A scene marked
 * [isEnding] = `true` describes an *authored* ending ("you win", "you
 * retire"); the death screen is shown automatically when the player's
 * `health` reaches `0` and is **not** one of the scenes.
 */
@Serializable
public data class Scene(
    public val id: SceneId,
    public val text: String,
    public val effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
    public val choices: List<Choice> = emptyList(),
    public val gate: Gate? = null,
    @SerialName("is_ending")
    public val isEnding: Boolean = false,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlin.jvm.JvmInline

/**
 * Stable identifier of a scene within an adventure.
 *
 * Wraps a [String] so that `Choice.nextScene` (a scene reference) cannot be
 * accidentally confused with a flag name, a stat name, or any other plain
 * string. Zero runtime cost — `@JvmInline value class` is erased to the
 * underlying `String` on JVM.
 *
 * **Serialized transparently** as the underlying string. `SceneId("start")`
 * appears in JSON as `"start"`, not as `{"value":"start"}`. This is what
 * `kotlinx.serialization` does for `@JvmInline value class` by default and
 * matches the current adventure file format.
 *
 * **Uniqueness** is enforced by the type checker (Ф2), not by the type
 * itself: two scenes could still be constructed with the same `SceneId`.
 *
 * Other IDs (`ChoiceId`, `ChapterId`, `VariableName`) are intentionally
 * plain `String` for now — a `SceneId` is the most frequent source of
 * confusion (`nextScene` vs a flag/stat name), so it gets the strongest
 * typing. Add value classes to the others only if the same confusion
 * materializes there.
 */
@Serializable
@JvmInline
public value class SceneId(public val value: String)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir

import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Declared type of a variable used in an adventure.
 *
 * The type is what the type checker (Ф2) uses to validate that references
 * in [Condition] and [Effect] are consistent with each other. For example,
 * a `has_sword` condition requires `sword` to be of type [Bool] or
 * [ItemCount]; a `health >= 50` comparison requires `health` to be
 * [Integer] or [IntRange].
 *
 * **Default values** (used when a variable is not present in
 * [InitialState], e.g. before the first scene that sets it):
 *
 * - [Bool] → `false`
 * - [Integer] → `0`
 * - [IntRange] → [IntRange.min] (the lowest allowed value)
 * - [ItemCount] → `0`
 * - [ItemList] → `emptyList()`
 */
@Serializable
public sealed class VarType {

    /** Boolean flag. `true`/`false`. */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("bool")
    public data object Bool : VarType()

    /**
     * Whole number without bounds. Used for stats like stamina or mana
     * that are allowed to go negative.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("int")
    public data object Integer : VarType()

    /**
     * Whole number clamped to `[min, max]`. Used for stats like health
     * that must stay within a sensible range.
     *
     * @property min lowest allowed value (inclusive).
     * @property max highest allowed value (inclusive).
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("int_range")
    public data class IntRange(
        public val min: Int,
        public val max: Int,
    ) : VarType()

    /**
     * Count of a stackable item (e.g. "3 potions"). Non-negative
     * [Integer] by semantics; kept as a separate type so the type checker
     * can distinguish "how many" from "any number".
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("item_count")
    public data object ItemCount : VarType()

    /**
     * Unordered list of item identifiers. Used for inventory-like
     * variables when the order does not matter.
     *
     * Not to be confused with [ItemCount], which is a single number.
     */
    @Serializable
    @SerialName("item_list")
    public data object ItemList : VarType()
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/parse/ConditionParser.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition

/**
 * Parses a condition string into a [Condition] AST node.
 *
 * **Syntactic only.** This parser knows nothing about variable types or
 * declared variables — that is the type checker's job (Ф2.2). It accepts
 * `has_sword` and produces [Condition.Has] even if `sword` is declared as
 * `ItemCount`; Ф2.2 rejects that with a hint to use `sword > 0` instead.
 *
 * **Grammar supported in Ф1.3:**
 *
 * | Input              | Result                                |
 * |--------------------|---------------------------------------|
 * | `has_X`            | `Condition.Has("X")`                  |
 * | `!has_X`           | `Condition.Not(Has("X"))`             |
 * | `X >= N`           | `Condition.Compare("X", GE, N)`       |
 * | `X > N`            | `Condition.Compare("X", GT, N)`       |
 * | `X <= N`           | `Condition.Compare("X", LE, N)`       |
 * | `X < N`            | `Condition.Compare("X", LT, N)`       |
 * | `X == N`           | `Condition.Compare("X", EQ, N)`       |
 * | `X != N`           | `Condition.Compare("X", NE, N)`       |
 *
 * Whitespace around `X`, the operator, and `N` is ignored. `N` may be
 * negative (`-10`). `X` may contain spaces (`"my stat >= 0"` is valid) —
 * this matches the current reader behaviour where
 * `condition.removePrefix("has_").trim()` keeps interior spaces.
 *
 * **Not supported yet (planned for Ф3.2 / N7.base):** `&&`, `||`, `!X`
 * (general negation), parentheses, `X in a..b`. Passing `"a && b"` today
 * returns a [ParseError.ConditionError]; it will parse in Ф3.2.
 */
public object ConditionParser {

    /**
     * Parses [input] as a single condition.
     *
     * @return [ParseResult.Success] with the AST node, or
     *   [ParseResult.Failure] with exactly one [ParseError.ConditionError].
     */
    /**
     * Characters reserved for future operators (`&&`, `||`, `!`, comparisons,
     * parentheses — planned for Ф3.2 / N7.base). A flag name must not contain
     * them: `has_sword && health` is not "a flag named 'sword && health'",
     * it is unsupported syntax. Accepting it silently would hide the error.
     */
    private val RESERVED_CHARS: Set<Char> = setOf('&', '|', '!', '<', '>', '=', '(', ')')

    public fun parse(input: String): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val s = input.trim()
        if (s.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Empty condition string", input, 0)
        }

        // 1. `!has_X` — negation of a boolean flag
        if (s.startsWith("!has_")) {
            val name = s.removePrefix("!has_").trim()
            if (name.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing variable name after '!has_'", input, 0)
            }
            checkNoReservedChars(name, input, "Flag name")?.let { return it }
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Not(Condition.Has(name)))
        }

        // 2. `has_X` — boolean flag
        if (s.startsWith("has_")) {
            val name = s.removePrefix("has_").trim()
            if (name.isEmpty()) {
                return fail("Missing variable name after 'has_'", input, 0)
            }
            checkNoReservedChars(name, input, "Flag name")?.let { return it }
            return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Has(name))
        }

        // 3. Comparison. Order matters: check two-character operators first,
        // so that `>=` is not consumed as `>` with `= ...`.
        val twoCharOps = listOf(
            ">=" to CompareOp.GE,
            "<=" to CompareOp.LE,
            "==" to CompareOp.EQ,
            "!=" to CompareOp.NE,
        )
        for ((token, op) in twoCharOps) {
            val idx = s.indexOf(token)
            if (idx >= 0) return buildCompare(s, token, op, input, idx)
        }

        val oneCharOps = listOf(
            ">" to CompareOp.GT,
            "<" to CompareOp.LT,
        )
        for ((token, op) in oneCharOps) {
            val idx = s.indexOf(token)
            if (idx >= 0) return buildCompare(s, token, op, input, idx)
        }

        return fail(
            "Unrecognized condition syntax: '$s'. " +
                    "Expected 'has_X', '!has_X', or 'X <op> N' where <op> is one of " +
                    ">=, >, <=, <, ==, !=.",
            input,
            0,
        )
    }

    private fun buildCompare(
        s: String,
        token: String,
        op: CompareOp,
        input: String,
        idx: Int,
    ): ParseResult<Condition> {
        val varName = s.substring(0, idx).trim()
        val valuePart = s.substring(idx + token.length).trim()

        if (varName.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Missing variable name before '$token'", input, idx)
        }
        checkNoReservedChars(varName, input, "Variable name")?.let { return it }
        if (valuePart.isEmpty()) {
            return fail("Missing integer value after '$token'", input, idx + token.length)
        }
        val value = valuePart.toIntOrNull()
            ?: return fail(
                "Expected integer value after '$token', got '$valuePart'",
                input,
                idx + token.length,
            )
        return ParseResult.Success(Condition.Compare(varName, op, value))
    }

    private fun checkNoReservedChars(
        value: String,
        input: String,
        forWhat: String,
    ): ParseResult.Failure? {
        val bad = value.firstOrNull { it in RESERVED_CHARS }
        if (bad != null) {
            return fail(
                "$forWhat '$value' contains reserved character '$bad'. " +
                        "Logical operators (&&, ||, !), comparisons, and parentheses " +
                        "are not supported yet (planned for Ф3.2 / N7.base).",
                input,
                0,
            )
        }
        return null
    }

    private fun fail(message: String, input: String, position: Int): ParseResult.Failure =
        ParseResult.Failure(listOf(ParseError.ConditionError(message, input, position)))
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/parse/ParseError.kt

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

/**
 * A single error produced by the JSON parser ([JsonToIr]) or by the
 * condition parser ([ConditionParser]).
 *
 * The parser never throws. It accumulates errors and returns them all at
 * once in [ParseResult.Failure], so that the editor and the analyzer can
 * show the author every problem in one pass instead of one at a time.
 *
 * **Not** `@Serializable`: parse errors are an API for the caller, not part
 * of the on-disk format. If they ever need to be persisted (e.g. in a
 * validation report), serialize them separately.
 */
public sealed class ParseError {

    /** Human-readable, English, one sentence. */
    public abstract val message: String

    /**
     * JSON-level syntax error: malformed input, unknown field with
     * strict mode, wrong type for a well-known field.
     *
     * @property path JSON path to the offending value
     *   (e.g. `"chapters[0].scenes[2].choices[0].condition"`), when known.
     */
    public data class Syntax(
        override val message: String,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()

    /**
     * Structural problem that is not a JSON syntax error: empty chapter
     * list, blank scene id, empty `next_scene`, etc.
     *
     * @property path same convention as [Syntax.path].
     */
    public data class Structure(
        override val message: String,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()

    /**
     * Condition string could not be parsed into
     * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition].
     *
     * @property input the raw condition string from JSON.
     * @property position 0-based offset in [input] where the parser gave up,
     *   when determinable.
     * @property path JSON path to the offending condition
     *   (e.g. `"chapters[1:c2].scenes[0:start].choices[2].condition"`),
     *   filled in by [JsonToIr] when accumulating errors. `null` when the
     *   error came from a standalone [ConditionParser] call.
     */
    public data class ConditionError(
        override val message: String,
        public val input: String,
        public val position: Int? = null,
        public val path: String? = null,
    ) : ParseError()
}


================================================
FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/parse/ParseResult.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse

/**
 * Result of a parse operation: either a value of type [T] or a non-empty
 * list of [ParseError]s.
 *
 * Chosen over Kotlin's stdlib [Result] because:
 * - [Result.Failure] carries a single [Throwable], not a list of errors.
 * - Wrapping [ParseError] in an exception would lose the structured type
 *   (the caller wants to pattern-match on [ParseError.ConditionError] etc.).
 *
 * **Invariant:** [Failure.errors] is never empty. The parser returns
 * [Success] or [Failure] with at least one error, never both.
 */
public sealed class ParseResult<out T> {

    /** Successful parse. */
    public data class Success<T>(public val value: T) : ParseResult<T>()

    /** Failed parse with one or more errors. */
    public data class Failure(public val errors: List<ParseError>) : ParseResult<Nothing>()
}

FILE: engine/src/main/kotlin/format/JsonToIr.kt
