package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.AdventureDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.ChapterDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.ChoiceDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto.SceneDto
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.DeathScene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.InitialState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagDefinition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Gate
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ConditionParser
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseError
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlinx.serialization.SerializationException
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId

/**
 * Parses the adventure JSON file into the typed IR ([Adventure]).
 *
 * **Single entry point for JSON → IR.** This is the only public function
 * in `:engine` that turns raw JSON text into an [Adventure]. It is used by:
 * - the reader (`:app`, Ф1.7) to load an adventure for playing;
 * - the editor (`:app`, Ф9.2) to validate an author's in-progress JSON;
 * - the analyzer (Ф1.6) after parsing, to check reachability and duplicates;
 * - tests (`:engine`, Ф1.3.4, Ф1.4), including the real `test_adventure.json`
 *   shipped to users.
 *
 * Do **not** write a second parser alongside this one. If a new format is
 * needed (YAML, binary, a future JS runtime), either add a `parse` overload
 * here or create a new top-level `object <Format>ToIr` with the same
 * `ParseResult<Adventure>` contract. Two parsers with divergent behaviour
 * is exactly the bug N2/Ф3 exists to prevent.
 *
 * **Parser vs Analyzer boundary** (do not blur this):
 * - **Parser** (this object): "can the file be turned into an
 *   [Adventure]?" — syntax of JSON, syntax of conditions, blank required
 *   fields, empty chapters. Nothing about the **meaning** of the file.
 * - **Analyzer** (Ф1.6): "is the resulting IR coherent?" — reachability,
 *   duplicate `scene.id`, `next_scene` pointing to a missing scene,
 *   `has_X` on a numeric variable (type checker, Ф2.2).
 *
 * Consequence: a JSON file that parses **successfully** may still be
 * rejected by the analyzer. That is by design — the two layers answer
 * different questions, and mixing them would make both harder to test.
 *
 * **Error strategy** (decision B from Ф1.3.3):
 * - **JSON syntax errors** (malformed JSON, wrong type for a field) — the
 *   underlying decoder throws `SerializationException`; we catch it once
 *   and return a single [ParseError.Syntax]. These are rare in practice:
 *   the editor always emits valid JSON, authors do not hand-write it.
 * - **Semantic errors** (blank ids, empty chapters, unparseable
 *   conditions) — accumulated into a [ParseResult.Failure] with **all**
 *   errors at once. Authors see every problem in one pass, not one at a
 *   time. This is the common case, so it is worth the extra code.
 *
 * **`path` convention:** `chapters[i:<id>].scenes[j:<id>].choices[k]`,
 * with `:<id>` omitted when the id is blank. Example:
 * `chapters[1:forest].scenes[0:start].choices[2]`. The author sees the
 * chapter and scene by name in the editor error panel (Ф9.2), not just
 * an index.
 *
 * **Not in scope here** (deferred):
 * - Type checking of variables (`has_X` on numeric variable) — Ф2.2.
 * - Duplicate `scene.id` detection — Ф2 / `Analyzer`.
 * - `next_scene` reachability — Ф2 / `Analyzer`.
 * - Migration of `version < CURRENT_VERSION` — Ф5.3 (for now, files with
 *   no `version` get [Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION]; files with any `version`
 *   keep it as-is).
 */
public object JsonToIr {

    private val json: Json = Json {
        ignoreUnknownKeys = true
        coerceInputValues = true
    }

    /**
     * Parses [text] (raw JSON contents of an adventure file) into an
     * [Adventure], or returns [ParseResult.Failure] with one or more
     * [ParseError]s.
     */
    public fun parse(text: String): ParseResult<Adventure> {
        val dto: AdventureDto = try {
            json.decodeFromString<AdventureDto>(text)
        } catch (e: SerializationException) {
            return ParseResult.Failure(
                listOf(
                    ParseError.Syntax(
                        message = "Malformed JSON: ${e.message ?: "unknown syntax error"}",
                        path = null,
                    ),
                ),
            )
        }

        val errors = mutableListOf<ParseError>()
        val adventure = buildAdventure(dto, errors)
        return if (errors.isEmpty()) {
            ParseResult.Success(adventure)
        } else {
            ParseResult.Failure(errors)
        }
    }

    // ---------- DTO → IR ----------

    private fun buildAdventure(
        dto: AdventureDto,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Adventure {
        if (dto.chapters.isEmpty()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Adventure has no chapters",
                path = null,
            )
        }
        // Version migration (v1 → v2, Ф1.5.4): gates moved from chapters
        // to scenes. A v1 file has `chapter.required_steps`; the migration
        // moves `chapter[i].required_steps = N > 0` onto the **last scene
        // of chapter i-1** as `Gate(N)`. The first chapter's
        // `required_steps` is dropped (it was always 0 in practice; even if
        // set, there is no "previous chapter" to gate).
        //
        // Files without `version` (pre-IR) are treated as v1 — same
        // migration. Files with `version >= 2` have `required_steps` on
        // chapters only as a leftover; we ignore it (it should be absent in
        // a well-formed v2 file).
        val effectiveVersion = dto.version ?: 1
        val lastChapterIndex = dto.chapters.lastIndex
        val chapters = dto.chapters.mapIndexed { index, chapterDto ->
            buildChapter(
                dto = chapterDto,
                index = index,
                errors = errors,
                // v1 → v2: `chapter[i].required_steps = N > 0` means
                // "walk N steps to enter chapter i". In v2 the gate lives
                // on the **last scene of chapter i-1** (the scene the player
                // must leave to enter chapter i). So for chapter `index`
                // we pass `required_steps` of chapter `index + 1`.
                previousChapterLastSceneGate = if (index < lastChapterIndex && effectiveVersion < 2) {
                    dto.chapters[index + 1].requiredSteps
                        .takeIf { it > 0 }
                        ?.let { Gate(it) }
                } else {
                    null
                },
            )
        }
        val deathScene = dto.deathScene?.let { d ->
            DeathScene(
                id = SceneId(d.id),
                text = d.text,
                allowStepBack = d.allowStepBack,
                allowChapterRestart = d.allowChapterRestart,
                allowAdventureRestart = d.allowAdventureRestart,
            )
        }
        // start_scene: explicit since v3; migrated from chapters in v1/v2.
        // - explicit value wins (v3+);
        // - v1/v2 without explicit value: infer from chapters;
        // - v3+ without explicit value: structural error (the field is
        //   required from v3 onward); fall back to SceneId("") so that
        //   Adventure can still be constructed, but `errors` is non-empty,
        //   so `JsonToIr.parse` returns Failure and the IR is not used.
        val startScene = dto.startScene?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { SceneId(it) }
            ?: if (effectiveVersion < 3) {
                chapters.firstOrNull()?.scenes?.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId("")
            } else {
                errors += ParseError.Structure(
                    message = "Adventure has no start_scene (required since v3)",
                    path = null,
                )
                SceneId("")
            }
        return Adventure(
            version = dto.version ?: Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION,
            title = dto.title,
            author = dto.author,
            description = dto.description,
            variables = emptyMap(), // Ф2.8: variables are not in the JSON yet
            tags = dto.tags.map { t ->
                TagDefinition(
                    name = t.name,
                    displayName = t.displayName,
                    category = t.category,
                    visible = t.visible,
                )
            },
            initialState = InitialState(
                flags = dto.initialState.flags,
                stats = dto.initialState.stats,
            ),
            deathScene = deathScene,
            startScene = startScene,
            chapters = chapters,
        )
    }

    private fun buildChapter(
        dto: ChapterDto,
        index: Int,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
        /**
         * v1 → v2 migration: a non-null gate to attach to the **last scene**
         * of this chapter. This comes from `chapter[index+1].required_steps`
         * in a v1 file, or from `null` for v2 files (and for the last
         * chapter).
         */
        previousChapterLastSceneGate: Gate? = null,
    ): Chapter {
        val path = chapterPath(index, dto.id)
        if (dto.scenes.isEmpty()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Chapter has no scenes",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        val lastIndex = dto.scenes.lastIndex
        val scenes = dto.scenes.mapIndexed { sceneIndex, sceneDto ->
            val built = buildScene(sceneDto, path, sceneIndex, errors)
            // Apply v1 → v2 migration gate on the last scene of this chapter
            // (if any). A scene that already has its own gate wins — the
            // author's intent (v2) overrides the legacy (v1) interpretation.
            if (sceneIndex == lastIndex && previousChapterLastSceneGate != null && built.gate == null) {
                built.copy(gate = previousChapterLastSceneGate)
            } else {
                built
            }
        }
        return Chapter(
            id = dto.id,
            title = dto.title,
            scenes = scenes,
        )
    }

    private fun buildScene(
        dto: SceneDto,
        parentPath: String,
        index: Int,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Scene {
        val path = scenePath(parentPath, index, dto.id)
        if (dto.id.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Scene id is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        val effects = buildEffects(dto.setFlags, dto.removeFlags, dto.modifyStats)
        val choices = dto.choices.mapIndexed { choiceIndex, choiceDto ->
            buildChoice(choiceDto, dto.id, path, choiceIndex, errors)
        }
        val gate = dto.gate?.let { raw ->
            if (raw <= 0) {
                errors += ParseError.Structure(
                    message = "Scene gate must be a positive number of steps, got $raw",
                    path = "$path.gate",
                )
                null
            } else {
                // Ф1.7.0.4: identity migration v4 → v5. Old files have no
                // gate_repeatable; default is "once passed, stays passed
                // for this playthrough" — the least surprising mode for the
                // common "unlock the next chapter" case. Per-visit behaviour
                // is opt-in via "gate_repeatable": true.
                Gate(requiredSteps = raw, repeatable = dto.gateRepeatable ?: false)
            }
        }
        return Scene(
            id = SceneId(dto.id),
            text = dto.text,
            effects = effects,
            choices = choices,
            gate = gate,
            // Ф1.7.0: identity migration v3 → v4. Files that predate v4
            // have no is_ending field; treat as false. Files that carry
            // it use the value as written.
            isEnding = dto.isEnding ?: false,
        )
    }

    private fun buildChoice(
        dto: ChoiceDto,
        sceneId: String,
        parentPath: String,
        index: Int,
        errors: MutableList<ParseError>,
    ): Choice {
        val path = "$parentPath.choices[$index]"
        if (dto.text.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Choice text is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        if (dto.nextScene.isBlank()) {
            errors += ParseError.Structure(
                message = "Choice next_scene is blank",
                path = path,
            )
        }
        val condition = dto.condition?.let { raw ->
            when (val result = ConditionParser.parse(raw)) {
                is ParseResult.Success -> result.value
                is ParseResult.Failure -> {
                    result.errors.forEach { err ->
                        errors += if (err is ParseError.ConditionError) {
                            err.copy(path = "$path.condition")
                        } else {
                            err
                        }
                    }
                    null
                }
            }
        }
        val effects = buildEffects(dto.setFlags, dto.removeFlags, dto.modifyStats)
        val choiceId = dto.id?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
            ?.let { ChoiceId(it) }
            ?: ChoiceId("${sceneId}_choice_$index")
        return Choice(
            id = choiceId,
            text = dto.text,
            nextScene = SceneId(dto.nextScene),
            condition = condition,
            effects = effects,
        )
    }

    /**
     * Flattens the three parallel JSON fields into a single ordered
     * [Effect] list. Order matches the current reader:
     * `set_flags` first, then `remove_flags`, then `modify_stats`.
     * `modify_stats` order follows the JSON object's key order
     * (`LinkedHashMap` in `kotlinx.serialization`).
     */
    private fun buildEffects(
        setFlags: List<String>,
        removeFlags: List<String>,
        modifyStats: Map<String, Int>,
    ): List<Effect> {
        val result = mutableListOf<Effect>()
        setFlags.forEach { result += Effect.SetFlag(it) }
        removeFlags.forEach { result += Effect.RemoveFlag(it) }
        modifyStats.forEach { (name, delta) -> result += Effect.ModifyStat(name, delta) }
        return result
    }

    // ---------- Path helpers ----------

    private fun chapterPath(index: Int, id: String): String =
        if (id.isBlank()) "chapters[$index]" else "chapters[$index:$id]"

    private fun scenePath(parentPath: String, index: Int, id: String): String =
        if (id.isBlank()) "$parentPath.scenes[$index]"
        else "$parentPath.scenes[$index:$id]"
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.dto

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.TagCategory
import kotlinx.serialization.SerialName
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Wire-format DTOs for the adventure JSON.
 *
 * These classes mirror the on-disk JSON exactly. They are **internal** —
 * a detail of the [com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr] pipeline,
 * not part of `:engine`'s public API. The public API works with
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure] and friends.
 *
 * All optional fields use non-null defaults (`emptyList()`, `emptyMap()`,
 * `null` for nullable types) so that the mapper does not have to write
 * `?: emptyList()` at every call site. `Json { coerceInputValues = true }`
 * (configured in `JsonToIr`) makes an explicit `null` in JSON behave the
 * same as a missing field.
 *
 * **Exception:** [AdventureDto.version] is nullable on purpose. `null`
 * means "the file has no version field" → the parser substitutes
 * [com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure.CURRENT_VERSION]. We must be
 * able to distinguish "no version" from any explicit integer.
 *
 * **Deferred to Ф2.8:** `variables` (`Map<String, VarDeclDto>`). Not
 * present in `test_adventure.json` yet; add when the file gains it.
 *
 * **Why one file:** DTOs form a single JSON contract and change together;
 * splitting them across seven files would add navigation noise without any
 * benefit. This is an intentional exception to the "one class per file"
 * convention, not an accident.
 */
@Serializable
internal data class AdventureDto(
    val version: Int? = null,
    val title: String,
    val author: String = "",
    val description: String = "",
    @SerialName("initial_state")
    val initialState: InitialStateDto = InitialStateDto(),
    val tags: List<TagDefinitionDto> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("death_scene")
    val deathScene: DeathSceneDto? = null,
    /** v3+; absent in v1/v2 files (migrated in `JsonToIr`). */
    @SerialName("start_scene")
    val startScene: String? = null,
    val chapters: List<ChapterDto> = emptyList(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class ChapterDto(
    val id: String,
    val title: String = "",
    /**
     * **Legacy (v1).** In adventure files of version 1 this field carried
     * a step gate on the chapter. Since v2 the gate lives on the scene
     * ([SceneDto.gate]). Kept here so v1 files still parse; `JsonToIr`
     * migrates a non-zero value onto the last scene of the previous
     * chapter as `Gate(requiredSteps)`.
     */
    @SerialName("required_steps")
    val requiredSteps: Int = 0,
    val scenes: List<SceneDto> = emptyList(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class SceneDto(
    val id: String,
    val text: String,
    @SerialName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    val choices: List<ChoiceDto> = emptyList(),
    val gate: Int? = null,
    /**
     * v5+; absent in v1–v4 files. `null` means "field was not in the
     * source file". `JsonToIr` maps `null` to `false` (identity
     * migration v4 → v5). Adventure file format keeps the gate flat:
     * `"gate": N` + optional `"gate_repeatable": true`, so a simple
     * gate stays one key.
     */
    @SerialName("gate_repeatable")
    val gateRepeatable: Boolean? = null,
    /**
     * v4+; absent in v1–v3 files. `null` means "field was not in the
     * source file". `JsonToIr` maps `null` to `false` (identity
     * migration v3 → v4). Nullable rather than `Boolean = false` for
     * consistency with [AdventureDto.version] and [SceneDto.gate], and
     * so that a future migration can distinguish "author explicitly
     * wrote `is_ending: false`" from "author did not write the field".
     * Today both collapse to `Scene.isEnding = false`, so the
     * distinction is not observed.
     */
    @SerialName("is_ending")
    val isEnding: Boolean? = null,
)

@Serializable
internal data class ChoiceDto(
    val id: String? = null,
    val text: String,
    @SerialName("next_scene")
    val nextScene: String,
    val condition: String? = null,
    @SerialName("set_flags")
    val setFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("remove_flags")
    val removeFlags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    @SerialName("modify_stats")
    val modifyStats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class TagDefinitionDto(
    val name: String,
    @SerialName("display_name")
    val displayName: String = "",
    val category: TagCategory = TagCategory.JOURNAL,
    val visible: Boolean = false,
)

@Serializable
internal data class InitialStateDto(
    val flags: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
)

@Serializable
internal data class DeathSceneDto(
    val id: String = "death_scene",
    val text: String = "💀 Вы погибли.",
    @SerialName("allow_step_back")
    val allowStepBack: Boolean = true,
    @SerialName("allow_chapter_restart")
    val allowChapterRestart: Boolean = true,
    @SerialName("allow_adventure_restart")
    val allowAdventureRestart: Boolean = true,
)

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Effect
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.PlayerState
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals

class EffectsApplierTest {

    @Test
    fun `empty effects return same state`() {
        val s = PlayerState(flags = setOf("a"), stats = mapOf("health" to 10))
        assertEquals(s, EffectsApplier.apply(s, emptyList()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `set flag adds`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(),
            listOf(Effect.SetFlag("a"), Effect.SetFlag("b")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("a", "b"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `set flag is idempotent`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(flags = setOf("a")),
            listOf(Effect.SetFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("a"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `remove flag removes`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(flags = setOf("a", "b")),
            listOf(Effect.RemoveFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("b"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `modify stat adds delta`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -30)),
        )
        assertEquals(70, s.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `modify stat creates missing with delta`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(),
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("mana", 5)),
        )
        assertEquals(5, s.stats["mana"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `modify stat clamps to zero`() {
        // Ф1.5 policy: all ModifyStat clamp to >= 0. In Ф2.8 this becomes
        // type-dependent (HEALTH/ITEM clamp, Integer/IntRange per-type).
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 3)),
            listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10)),
        )
        assertEquals(0, s.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `order matters - remove then set leaves set`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(flags = setOf("a")),
            listOf(Effect.RemoveFlag("a"), Effect.SetFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(setOf("a"), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `order matters - set then remove leaves unset`() {
        val s = EffectsApplier.apply(
            PlayerState(),
            listOf(Effect.SetFlag("a"), Effect.RemoveFlag("a")),
        )
        assertEquals(emptySet(), s.flags)
    }

    @Test
    fun `state is not mutated`() {
        val original = PlayerState(stats = mapOf("health" to 10))
        EffectsApplier.apply(original, listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -5)))
        assertEquals(10, original.stats["health"])
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Choice
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.ChoiceId
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertTrue


class EngineCompileTest {

    private fun adventure(vararg chapters: Chapter): Adventure = Adventure(
        title = "T",
        startScene = chapters.firstOrNull()?.scenes?.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId(""),
        chapters = chapters.toList(),
    )

    private fun chapter(id: String, vararg scenes: Scene): Chapter = Chapter(
        id = id,
        title = id,
        scenes = scenes.toList(),
    )

    private fun scene(id: String): Scene = Scene(id = SceneId(id), text = "x")

    @Test
    fun `single scene compiles`() {
        val adv = adventure(chapter("c1", scene("s1")))
        val result = Engine.compile(adv)
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(result).compiled
        assertEquals(1, compiled.scenesById.size)
        assertEquals("s1", compiled.scenesById[SceneId("s1")]?.id?.value)
        assertEquals(0, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s1")])
    }

    @Test
    fun `multiple chapters compile`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            chapter("c1", scene("s1"), scene("s2")),
            chapter("c2", scene("s3")),
        )
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adv)).compiled
        assertEquals(3, compiled.scenesById.size)
        assertEquals(0, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s1")])
        assertEquals(0, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s2")])
        assertEquals(1, compiled.chapterIndexBySceneId[SceneId("s3")])
    }

    @Test
    fun `duplicate scene id fails with chapter indices`() {
        val adv = adventure(
            chapter("c1", scene("s1")),
            chapter("c2", scene("s1")),
        )
        val result = Engine.compile(adv)
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(result).errors
        val duplicate = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.DuplicateSceneId>().single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("s1"), duplicate.sceneId)
        assertEquals(listOf(0, 1), duplicate.chapterIndices)
        assertTrue(duplicate.message.contains("chapters 1, 2"), duplicate.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing start scene fails compile`() {
        // startScene points to "ghost"; the only scene is "s1".
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("ghost"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("c1", scene("s1"))),
        )
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(Engine.compile(adv)).errors
        val missing = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.MissingStartScene>().single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("ghost"), missing.startSceneId)
        assertTrue(missing.message.contains("ghost"), missing.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing next_scene fails compile with choice details`() {
        val a = Scene(
            id = SceneId("a"),
            text = "text of a",
            choices = listOf(
                Choice(
                    id = ChoiceId("c1"),
                    text = "Go",
                    nextScene = SceneId("ghost"),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("a"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("ch", a)),
        )
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(Engine.compile(adv)).errors
        val missing = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.MissingNextScene>().single()
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), missing.sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c1"), missing.choiceId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("ghost"), missing.targetSceneId)
        assertTrue(missing.message.contains("c1"), missing.message)
        assertTrue(missing.message.contains("ghost"), missing.message)
    }

    @Test
    fun `multiple missing next_scene errors are reported in stable order`() {
        val a = Scene(
            id = SceneId("a"),
            text = "text of a",
            choices = listOf(
                Choice(id = ChoiceId("c1"), text = "Go", nextScene = SceneId("ghost1")),
                Choice(id = ChoiceId("c2"), text = "Go", nextScene = SceneId("ghost2")),
            ),
        )
        val b = Scene(
            id = SceneId("b"),
            text = "text of b",
            choices = listOf(
                Choice(id = ChoiceId("c1"), text = "Go", nextScene = SceneId("ghost3")),
            ),
        )
        val adv = Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId("a"),
            chapters = listOf(chapter("ch", a, b)),
        )
        val errors = assertIs<CompileResult.Failure>(Engine.compile(adv)).errors
        val missing = errors.filterIsInstance<CompileError.MissingNextScene>()
        assertEquals(3, missing.size)
        // Sorted by (sceneId, choiceId): a/c1, a/c2, b/c1.
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), missing[0].sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c1"), missing[0].choiceId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("a"), missing[1].sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c2"), missing[1].choiceId)
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), missing[2].sceneId)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("c1"), missing[2].choiceId)
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.format.JsonToIr
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Chapter

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Gate
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.PlayerState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Scene
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.SceneId
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.toPlayerState
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompiledAdventure
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertNotNull
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class EngineStepTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun scene(
        id: String,
        choices: List<Choice> = emptyList(),
        gate: Gate? = null,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
    ): Scene = Scene(
        id = SceneId(id),
        text = "text of $id",
        effects = effects,
        choices = choices,
        gate = gate,
    )

    private fun choice(
        id: String,
        next: String,
        condition: Condition? = null,
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
    ): Choice = Choice(
        id = ChoiceId(id),
        text = "choice $id",
        nextScene = SceneId(next),
        condition = condition,
        effects = effects,
    )

    private fun chapter(id: String, vararg scenes: Scene): Chapter =
        Chapter(id = id, title = id, scenes = scenes.toList())

    private fun adventure(vararg chapters: Chapter): Adventure = Adventure(
        title = "T",
        startScene = chapters.firstOrNull()?.scenes?.firstOrNull()?.id ?: SceneId(""),
        chapters = chapters.toList(),
    )

    private fun compile(adventure: Adventure): CompiledAdventure =
        assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

    private fun state(
        flags: Set<String> = emptySet(),
        stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    ): PlayerState = PlayerState(flags = flags, stats = stats)

    private fun rejected(result: StepResult): RejectReason =
        assertIs<StepResult.Rejected>(result, "expected Rejected, got $result").reason

    // ---------- happy path ----------

    @Test
    fun `simple transition succeeds and returns target scene`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))
        val initial = state()

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, initial, SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), success.currentScene.id)
        assertEquals(false, success.isDead)
        assertEquals(initial, success.state)
    }

    @Test
    fun `choice effects applied to state`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            listOf(
                choice(
                    "c",
                    next = "b",
                    effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10)),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(
            compiled,
            state(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            SceneId("a"),
            ChoiceId("c"),
        )
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(90, success.state.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `state is not mutated`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            listOf(choice("c", next = "b", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10)))),
        )
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))
        val initial = state(stats = mapOf("health" to 100))

        Engine.step(compiled, initial, SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))

        assertEquals(100, initial.stats["health"], "original state must not be mutated")
    }

    @Test
    fun `effects applied in list order`() {
        // Set then remove: flag absent. If order were reversed, flag present.
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            listOf(
                choice(
                    "c",
                    next = "b",
                    effects = listOf(Effect.SetFlag("x"), Effect.RemoveFlag("x")),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertTrue("x" !in success.state.flags)
    }

    // ---------- structural errors ----------

    @Test
    fun `scene not found`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "a")))
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a)))

        val reason = rejected(
            Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("missing"), ChoiceId("c")),
        )
        assertIs<RejectReason.SceneNotFound>(reason)
        assertEquals(SceneId("missing"), reason.sceneId)
    }

    @Test
    fun `choice not found`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "a")))
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a)))

        val reason = rejected(
            Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("other")),
        )
        assertIs<RejectReason.ChoiceNotFound>(reason)
        assertEquals(ChoiceId("other"), reason.choiceId)
    }

    @Test
    fun `next scene not found - bug`() {
        // Engine.compile rejects this (Ф1.6.2.1:
        // CompileError.MissingNextScene), so in production the reader
        // never sees this state. But CompiledAdventure is a public data
        // class; anyone can construct one by hand (tests, future tooling).
        // This test documents that Engine.step is **defensive**: with a
        // manually-built CompiledAdventure that has a dangling nextScene,
        // step returns Rejected(SceneNotFound) and does NOT apply choice
        // effects (otherwise the player's health would drain into the void
        // before the reader notices the missing scene).
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            listOf(
                choice("c", next = "ghost", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -50))),
            ),
        )
        val adv = adventure(chapter("ch", a))
        val compiled = CompiledAdventure(
            adventure = adv,
            scenesById = mapOf(SceneId("a") to a),
            chapterIndexBySceneId = mapOf(SceneId("a") to 0),
        )

        val reason = rejected(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
                SceneId("a"),
                ChoiceId("c"),
            ),
        )
        assertIs<RejectReason.SceneNotFound>(reason)
        assertEquals(SceneId("ghost"), reason.sceneId)
    }

    // ---------- blockers: condition ----------

    @Test
    fun `condition passes - success`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            listOf(
                choice(
                    "c",
                    next = "b",
                    condition = Condition.Compare("health", com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp.GE, 50),
                ),
            ),
        )
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(
            compiled,
            state(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            SceneId("a"),
            ChoiceId("c"),
        )
        assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
    }

    @Test
    fun `condition fails - blocked with ConditionNotMet`() {
        val condition = Condition.Compare("health", com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp.GE, 50)
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b", condition = condition)))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val reason = rejected(
            Engine.step(compiled, state(stats = mapOf("health" to 10)), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c")),
        )
        val blocked = assertIs<RejectReason.Blocked>(reason)
        assertEquals(1, blocked.blockers.size)
        val blocker = assertIs<Blocker.ConditionNotMet>(blocked.blockers[0])
        assertEquals(condition, blocker.condition)
    }

    // ---------- blockers: gate ----------

    @Test
    fun `gate passed - success`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")), gate = Gate(100))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(
            compiled,
            state(),
            SceneId("a"),
            ChoiceId("c"),
            stepsInScene = 150,
        )
        assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
    }

    @Test
    fun `gate not passed - blocked with remaining`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")), gate = Gate(100))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val reason = rejected(
            Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"), stepsInScene = 40),
        )
        val blocked = assertIs<RejectReason.Blocked>(reason)
        val gateBlocker = assertIs<Blocker.GateNotPassed>(blocked.blockers.single())
        assertEquals(60, gateBlocker.remainingSteps)
    }

    @Test
    fun `gate present and stepsInScene null - safe default blocked`() {
        // null = "unknown". Treated as 0 walked, so gate blocks with full remaining.
        // Safety: a caller that forgets to pass steps cannot bypass the gate.
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")), gate = Gate(100))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val reason = rejected(
            Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"), stepsInScene = null),
        )
        val blocked = assertIs<RejectReason.Blocked>(reason)
        assertEquals(100, (blocked.blockers.single() as Blocker.GateNotPassed).remainingSteps)
    }

    @Test
    fun `no gate and stepsInScene null - ignored`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"), stepsInScene = null)
        assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
    }

    // ---------- multiple blockers ----------

    @Test
    fun `condition and gate both fail - all blockers reported in order`() {
        val condition = Condition.Compare("health", com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp.GE, 50)
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b", condition = condition)), gate = Gate(100))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val reason = rejected(
            Engine.step(compiled, state(stats = mapOf("health" to 10)), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"), stepsInScene = 30),
        )
        val blocked = assertIs<RejectReason.Blocked>(reason)
        assertEquals(2, blocked.blockers.size)
        assertIs<Blocker.ConditionNotMet>(blocked.blockers[0])
        assertIs<Blocker.GateNotPassed>(blocked.blockers[1])
        assertEquals(70, (blocked.blockers[1] as Blocker.GateNotPassed).remainingSteps)
    }

    // ---------- death by choice effects ----------

    @Test
    fun `choice effects kill player - isDead true`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            listOf(
                choice("c", next = "b", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -999))),
            ),
        )
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(
            compiled,
            state(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            SceneId("a"),
            ChoiceId("c"),
        )
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertTrue(success.isDead)
        assertEquals(0, success.state.stats["health"]) // clamped
    }

    @Test
    fun `choice effects do not kill - isDead false`() {
        val a = scene(
            "a",
            listOf(choice("c", next = "b", effects = listOf(Effect.ModifyStat("health", -10)))),
        )
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(
            compiled,
            state(stats = mapOf("health" to 100)),
            SceneId("a"),
            ChoiceId("c"),
        )
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(false, success.isDead)
        assertEquals(90, success.state.stats["health"])
    }

    @Test
    fun `no health declared - not dead`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(false, success.isDead)
    }

    // ---------- cross-chapter ----------

    @Test
    fun `cross-chapter transition - success`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c", next = "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(adventure(chapter("ch1", a), chapter("ch2", b)))

        val result = Engine.step(compiled, state(), SceneId("a"), ChoiceId("c"))
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(result)
        assertEquals(SceneId("b"), success.currentScene.id)
    }

    // ---------- real test_adventure.json: documented pre-Continue state ----------

    @Test
    fun `chapter_end_1 has explicit Continue choice - player can proceed after gate`() {
        // Ф1.5.5.0: chapter_end_1 and chapter_end_2 now have explicit
        // "Continue" choices. This is the "test first, then fix" pattern:
        // the previous test asserted "no choices"; after the fix, the
        // scene must have exactly one Continue choice, and step() with it
        // must succeed once the gate (5 steps) is passed.
        val json = loadResource("/test_adventure.json")
        val parseResult = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val adventure = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(parseResult).value
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

        val chapterEnd1 = assertNotNull(compiled.scenesById[SceneId("chapter_end_1")])
        assertEquals(1, chapterEnd1.choices.size, "chapter_end_1 should have one Continue choice")
        val continueChoice = chapterEnd1.choices.single()
        assertEquals("Продолжить", continueChoice.text)
        assertEquals(SceneId("conditions_test"), continueChoice.nextScene)

        // Gate 1 (Ф1.7.0.4 simplified all test gates to 1 step so the
        // reference sample can be checked by walking — one step is
        // enough to exercise the mechanic). stepsInScene = 0 → blocked.
        val blocked = rejected(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state = adventure.initialState.toPlayerState(),
                sceneId = SceneId("chapter_end_1"),
                choiceId = continueChoice.id,
                stepsInScene = 0,
            ),
        )
        val blockedReason = assertIs<RejectReason.Blocked>(blocked)
        assertEquals(1, (blockedReason.blockers.single() as Blocker.GateNotPassed).remainingSteps)

        // Gate 1, stepsInScene = 1 → success, moves to conditions_test.
        val success = assertIs<StepResult.Success>(
            Engine.step(
                compiled,
                state = adventure.initialState.toPlayerState(),
                sceneId = SceneId("chapter_end_1"),
                choiceId = continueChoice.id,
                stepsInScene = 1,
            ),
        )
        assertEquals(SceneId("conditions_test"), success.currentScene.id)
    }

    @Test
    fun `chapter_end_2 has explicit Continue choice going to final`() {
        val json = loadResource("/test_adventure.json")
        val parseResult = JsonToIr.parse(json)
        val adventure = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(parseResult).value
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

        val chapterEnd2 = assertNotNull(compiled.scenesById[SceneId("chapter_end_2")])
        assertEquals(1, chapterEnd2.choices.size)
        val continueChoice = chapterEnd2.choices.single()
        assertEquals("Продолжить", continueChoice.text)
        assertEquals(SceneId("final"), continueChoice.nextScene)
    }

    private fun loadResource(path: String): String {
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream(path)
            ?: error("Resource '$path' not found on classpath")
        return stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.CompareOp
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Condition
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.PlayerState
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertFalse
import kotlin.test.assertTrue

class EvaluatorTest {

    private fun state(
        flags: Set<String> = emptySet(),
        stats: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
    ): PlayerState = PlayerState(flags = flags, stats = stats)

    @Test
    fun `has flag true when present`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("sword"))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Has("sword"), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `has flag false when absent`() {
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Has("sword"), state()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `has does not look at stats - sword in stats but not flags is false`() {
        // Regression for the Ф1.5 decision: `has_X` is only for Bool flags.
        // `sword` in `stats` (ItemCount) is NOT a flag; type checker in
        // Ф2.2 will reject `has_sword` on `sword: ItemCount`, but until
        // then the evaluator is strict.
        val s = state(stats = mapOf("sword" to 1))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Has("sword"), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `not inverts`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("sword"))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("sword")), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Not(Condition.Has("bow")), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `and requires both`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("a"))
        assertTrue(
            Evaluator.evaluate(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Not(Condition.Has("b"))),
                s,
            ),
        )
        assertFalse(
            Evaluator.evaluate(
                Condition.And(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                s,
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `or requires one`() {
        val s = state(flags = setOf("a"))
        assertTrue(
            Evaluator.evaluate(
                Condition.Or(Condition.Has("a"), Condition.Has("b")),
                s,
            ),
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare all operators`() {
        val s = state(stats = mapOf("health" to 50))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GE, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LE, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.EQ, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.NE, 49), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 49), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LT, 51), s))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.GT, 50), s))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("health", CompareOp.LT, 50), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `compare unknown stat defaults to zero`() {
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("mana", CompareOp.EQ, 0), state()))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("mana", CompareOp.GE, 0), state()))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.Compare("mana", CompareOp.GT, 0), state()))
    }

    @Test
    fun `in range inclusive`() {
        val s = state(stats = mapOf("health" to 50))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.InRange("health", 50, 50), s))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.InRange("health", 0, 100), s))
        assertFalse(Evaluator.evaluate(Condition.InRange("health", 51, 100), s))
    }

    @Test
    fun `is dead only when health at or below zero`() {
        assertFalse(Evaluator.isDead(state(stats = mapOf("health" to 1))))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.isDead(state(stats = mapOf("health" to 0))))
        assertTrue(Evaluator.isDead(state(stats = mapOf("health" to -5))))
    }

    @Test
    fun `is dead is false when health not declared`() {
        // "no health" means the adventure does not use death.
        assertFalse(Evaluator.isDead(state()))
    }
}

package com.myapp.adventure.engine.analyze

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.CompileResult

class AnalyzerTest {

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    private fun scene(
        id: String,
        choices: List<Choice> = emptyList(),
        effects: List<Effect> = emptyList(),
        isEnding: Boolean = false,
    ): Scene = Scene(
        id = SceneId(id),
        text = "text of $id",
        choices = choices,
        effects = effects,
        isEnding = isEnding,
    )

    private fun choice(
        id: String,
        next: String,
        condition: Condition? = null,
    ): Choice = Choice(
        id = ChoiceId(id),
        text = "to $next",
        nextScene = SceneId(next),
        condition = condition,
    )

    private fun chapter(id: String, vararg scenes: Scene): Chapter =
        Chapter(id = id, title = id, scenes = scenes.toList())

    private fun adventure(start: String, vararg chapters: Chapter): Adventure =
        Adventure(
            title = "T",
            startScene = SceneId(start),
            chapters = chapters.toList(),
        )

    private fun adventureWithLintSetup(
        start: String,
        tags: List<TagDefinition> = emptyList(),
        initialState: InitialState = InitialState(),
        deathScene: DeathScene? = null,
        vararg chapters: Chapter,
    ): Adventure = Adventure(
        title = "T",
        startScene = SceneId(start),
        tags = tags,
        initialState = initialState,
        deathScene = deathScene,
        chapters = chapters.toList(),
    )

    private fun itemTag(name: String): TagDefinition =
        TagDefinition(name = name, category = TagCategory.ITEM)

    private fun healthTag(name: String = "health"): TagDefinition =
        TagDefinition(name = name, category = TagCategory.HEALTH)

    private fun journalTag(name: String): TagDefinition =
        TagDefinition(name = name, category = TagCategory.JOURNAL)

    private fun compile(adventure: Adventure): CompiledAdventure =
        assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(Engine.compile(adventure)).compiled

    // ---------- reachable ----------

    @Test
    fun `linear chain - all scenes reachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b", listOf(choice("c2", "c")))
        val c = scene("c")
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b, c)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b"), SceneId("c")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("c")), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `orphan scene is unreachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val orphan = scene("orphan")
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b, orphan)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("orphan")), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("b")), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `cross-chapter transition is reachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b")
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure("a", chapter("ch1", a), chapter("ch2", b)),
        )

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
    }

    @Test
    fun `self-loop is reachable and terminates`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "a")))
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        // a has choices (self-loop), so it is not a dead end.
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `two-way cycle is reachable`() {
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b", listOf(choice("c2", "a")))
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, b)))

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a"), SceneId("b")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing start scene - everything unreachable`() {
        // Engine.compile rejects this (CompileError.MissingStartScene,
        // Ф1.6.2.1), so in production the reader never sees this state.
        // But CompiledAdventure is a public data class; anyone can
        // construct one by hand (tests, future tooling). This test
        // documents that Analyzer.reachable is **defensive**: with a
        // missing start scene, `reachable` is empty and every existing
        // scene is unreachable.
        val a = scene("a")
        val adv = adventure("ghost", chapter("ch", a))
        val compiled = CompiledAdventure(
            adventure = adv,
            scenesById = mapOf(SceneId("a") to a),
            chapterIndexBySceneId = mapOf(SceneId("a") to 0),
        )

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(emptySet(), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(listOf(SceneId("a")), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `nextScene to missing scene is not added to reachable`() {
        // Engine.compile rejects this (CompileError.MissingNextScene,
        // Ф1.6.2.1). Documenting Analyzer's defensive behaviour on a
        // manually-built CompiledAdventure: a missing target does not
        // enter `reachable` — it cannot be visited.
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "ghost")))
        val adv = adventure("a", chapter("ch", a))
        val compiled = CompiledAdventure(
            adventure = adv,
            scenesById = mapOf(SceneId("a") to a),
            chapterIndexBySceneId = mapOf(SceneId("a") to 0),
        )

        val report = Analyzer.reachable(compiled)
        assertEquals(setOf(SceneId("a")), report.reachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.unreachable)
        assertEquals(emptyList(), report.deadEnds)
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing nextScene does not produce a false unreachable lint`() {
        // Same setup as above; no lint issues. Missing references are
        // compile errors (Ф1.6.2.1), not lint issues. The analyzer sees a
        // valid CompiledAdventure with one dangling edge, but that edge
        // does not create a phantom scene, so nothing to lint.
        val a = scene("a", listOf(choice("c1", "ghost")))
        val adv = adventure("a", chapter("ch", a))
        val compiled = CompiledAdventure(
            adventure = adv,
            scenesById = mapOf(SceneId("a") to a),
            chapterIndexBySceneId = mapOf(SceneId("a") to 0),
        )

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report dead end on last scene of last chapter`() {
        // Ф1.7.0: "last scene of the last chapter" is no longer an
        // implicit ending — the scene must be explicitly marked.
        val a = scene("a", isEnding = true) // terminal, last scene, explicitly an ending
        val compiled = compile(adventure("a", chapter("ch", a)))

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint reports reachable dead end mid-adventure`() {
        val a = scene("a", choices = listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b") // terminal, reachable, not last scene
        val c = scene("c") // last scene, but unreachable from a
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure("a", chapter("ch1", a, b), chapter("ch2", c)),
        )

        val issues = Analyzer.lint(compiled)
        val kinds = issues.map { it.kind }
        assertTrue(LintKind.DeadEnd in kinds, "expected DeadEnd, got $kinds")
        assertTrue(
            LintKind.UnreachableScene in kinds,
            "expected UnreachableScene(c), got $kinds",
        )
        assertEquals(
            listOf(SceneId("b")),
            issues.filter { it.kind == LintKind.DeadEnd }.mapNotNull { it.sceneId },
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint does not report dead end on unreachable terminal scene`() {
        // Ф1.7.0: `b` must be explicitly marked as an ending, otherwise
        // the "last scene of the last chapter" convenience no longer
        // applies and DeadEnd(b) fires.
        val a = scene("a", choices = listOf(choice("c1", "b")))
        val b = scene("b", isEnding = true) // reachable, terminal, explicitly an ending
        val orphan = scene("orphan")         // unreachable, terminal, mid-chapter
        val compiled = compile(
            adventure("a", chapter("ch", a, orphan, b)),
        )

        val kinds = Analyzer.lint(compiled).map { it.kind }
        assertTrue(LintKind.UnreachableScene in kinds)
        assertTrue(
            LintKind.DeadEnd !in kinds,
            "unreachable terminal scene must not be double-flagged as DeadEnd: $kinds",
        )
    }

    @Test

            "mid",
            choices = listOf(
                choice("c1", "win"),
                choice("c2", "retire"),
            ),
        )
        val win = scene("win", isEnding = true)
        val retire = scene("retire", isEnding = true)
        val compiled = compile(adventure("mid", chapter("ch", mid, win, retire)))

        assertEquals(emptyList(), Analyzer.lint(compiled))
    }

    @Test
    fun `lint is clean on test_adventure_json`() {
        // test_adventure.json is the reference sample: every new user gets
        // it copied into their library on first launch. If the analyzer
        // flags something in it, either the sample is broken (fix the file)
        // or the new check is too aggressive (fix the check). This test is
        // the tripwire.
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream("/test_adventure.json")
            ?: error("test_adventure.json not on classpath")
        val raw = stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
        val adventure = assertIs<ParseResult.Success<Adventure>>(
            JsonToIr.parse(raw),
            "test_adventure.json must parse successfully",
        ).value
        val compiled = assertIs<CompileResult.Success>(
            Engine.compile(adventure),
            "test_adventure.json must compile successfully",
        ).compiled

        assertEquals(
            emptyList(),
            Analyzer.lint(compiled),
            "test_adventure.json must be lint-clean under current rules",
        )
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/test/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/format/GoldenIrTest.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonObject
import kotlin.test.Test
import kotlin.test.assertEquals
import kotlin.test.assertIs
import kotlin.test.assertTrue
import kotlin.test.fail

/**
 * Golden test for the IR: parses the real `test_adventure.json`, serializes
 * the resulting [Adventure] back to JSON, and compares **semantically**
 * against `engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json`.
 *
 * **Why this test exists:** every commit that changes the IR (adds, removes,
 * or renames a field) or the parser (changes how JSON becomes IR) can silently
 * break every adventure file in the wild. This test is the tripwire: **if
 * it fails and you did not intend to change the on-disk shape, you found a
 * bug**. If you did intend to change it, regenerate the golden with
 * `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden` and commit both.
 *
 * **Comparison is semantic, not textual.** `JsonElement`-tree equality
 * ignores whitespace, key order, and insignificant formatting. That means:
 * - Reformatting `golden_ir.json` in an IDE does not break the test.
 * - Reordering fields in JSON (Kotlin data class or `@SerialName`) does
 *   not break the test if the semantic structure is unchanged.
 * - A real semantic change (missing field, different value, different type)
 *   **does** break the test, with a diff that points at the exact spot.
 *
 * **Not `encodeDefaults = false` only.** The comparison uses the same
 * `PRETTY_JSON` config as [GoldenWriter] (`prettyPrint = true`,
 * `encodeDefaults = false`) so that both sides strip default-valued fields.
 * The golden file is human-readable (good for code review), and both sides
 * are normalized before comparison (good for stability).
 */
class GoldenIrTest {

    private val prettyJson: Json = Json {
        prettyPrint = true
        encodeDefaults = false
    }

    private fun loadText(path: String): String {
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream(path)
            ?: fail(
                "Resource '$path' not found on classpath.\n" +
                        "If '$path' is golden_ir.json, run:\n" +
                        "    ./gradlew :engine:updateGolden\n" +
                        "and commit the result.",
            )
        return stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
    }

    private fun parseRealAdventure(): Adventure {
        val raw = loadText("/test_adventure.json")
        val result = JsonToIr.parse(raw)
        return when (result) {
            is ParseResult.Success -> result.value
            is ParseResult.Failure -> fail(
                "test_adventure.json failed to parse: $result",
            )
        }
    }

    private fun currentIrAsJsonElement(): JsonElement {
        val adventure = parseRealAdventure()
        val text = prettyJson.encodeToString(Adventure.serializer(), adventure)
        return Json.parseToJsonElement(text)
    }

    @Test
    fun `golden matches current IR`() {
        val goldenText = loadText("/golden_ir.json")
        val golden = Json.parseToJsonElement(goldenText)
        val actual = currentIrAsJsonElement()

        if (golden == actual) return

        // Produce a readable diff for the failure message. We do not have a
        // full JSON diff here (would need a library), but we can show the
        // first top-level key that differs, which is usually enough to tell
        // "IR shape changed" from "one value changed".
        val diffHint = topLevelDiffHint(golden, actual)
        fail(
            "IR differs from golden_ir.json.\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "If you changed the IR (files in :engine/.../ir/), the parser\n" +
                    "(JsonToIr, ConditionParser), or test_adventure.json — and you\n" +
                    "**intended** the change — regenerate the golden:\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "    ./gradlew :engine:updateGolden\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "Then run `git diff engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json`\n" +
                    "to verify the change is exactly what you expected, and commit\n" +
                    "the golden alongside your code change.\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "If you did NOT intend any of the above — you found a bug.\n" +
                    "Investigate before running updateGolden.\n" +
                    "\n" +
                    "Hint: $diffHint",
        )
    }

    @Test
    fun `missing golden is a clear failure`() {
        // The `loadText` helper fails with the exact instruction to run
        // `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden`. This test exists so that the
        // failure mode is exercised by CI, not discovered manually when
        // someone deletes golden_ir.json by accident.
        //
        // We do not actually delete the golden in this test (that would race
        // with `golden matches current IR`). Instead, we assert that
        // `loadText` on a nonexistent path produces the expected instruction.
        val missingPath = "/this-file-does-not-exist-golden-ir-test.json"
        val stream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream(missingPath)
        assertEquals(null, stream, "sanity: missing path should be null")

        // And the real golden loads fine.
        val realStream = javaClass.getResourceAsStream("/golden_ir.json")
        assertTrue(
            realStream != null,
            "golden_ir.json should exist; if this fails, run ./gradlew :engine:updateGolden",
        )
        realStream.use { it.readBytes() }
    }

    @Test
    fun `golden round-trips through IR serializer`() {
        // Sanity: the golden file was written by `Adventure.serializer()`
        // and must be readable by the matching deserializer. This catches a
        // specific failure mode: `@Serializable` produces valid JSON that
        // cannot be read back (e.g. a polymorphic sealed class with a
        // missing `@SerialName`, or a value class serialized as an object
        // but expected as a string). If that happens, the golden file is
        // internally inconsistent — useful as documentation, dangerous as a
        // test fixture.
        //
        // **Note on format:** the golden is an **IR serialization**, not an
        // adventure file. `JsonToIr.parse` (adventure format) would fail on
        // it, because IR conditions are structured (`{"type":"has",...}`)
        // while adventure conditions are strings (`"has_sword"`). This test
        // uses `Json.decodeFromString<Adventure>` — the IR deserializer —
        // which is the correct counterpart to `GoldenWriter`.
        val goldenText = loadText("/golden_ir.json")
        val irJson = Json {
            ignoreUnknownKeys = true
            coerceInputValues = true
        }
        val adventure = irJson.decodeFromString<Adventure>(goldenText)
        assertEquals(3, adventure.chapters.size)
        assertEquals("Тестовое приключение", adventure.title)

        // And the re-encoded form must match the golden semantically:
        // decode → encode should not change the IR representation.
        val reEncoded = prettyJson.encodeToString(Adventure.serializer(), adventure)
        val reJson = Json.parseToJsonElement(reEncoded)
        val originalJson = Json.parseToJsonElement(goldenText)
        assertEquals(
            originalJson,
            reJson,
            "IR serialization is not stable through decode→encode",
        )
    }

    // ---------- diff helpers ----------

    private fun topLevelDiffHint(expected: JsonElement, actual: JsonElement): String {
        val e = expected as? JsonObject ?: return "expected is not a JSON object"
        val a = actual as? JsonObject ?: return "actual is not a JSON object"
        val keys = (e.keys + a.keys).sorted()
        for (k in keys) {
            val ev = e[k]
            val av = a[k]
            if (ev != av) {
                return when {
                    ev == null -> "field '$k' present in actual, missing in golden"
                    av == null -> "field '$k' present in golden, missing in actual"
                    ev is JsonPrimitive && av is JsonPrimitive ->
                        "field '$k' changed: golden=$ev, actual=$av"
                    else -> "field '$k' differs structurally (golden type=${ev::class.simpleName}, actual type=${av::class.simpleName})"
                }
            }
        }
        return "no top-level difference found (differs somewhere nested; check full output)"
    }
}

FILE: engine/src/test/kotlin/com/myapp/adventure/engine/format/GoldenWriter.kt
================================================
package com.myapp.adventure.engine.format

import com.myapp.adventure.engine.ir.Adventure
import com.myapp.adventure.engine.parse.ParseResult
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import java.io.File

/**
 * Regenerates `engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json` from the current
 * parser and the current `test_adventure.json`.
 *
 * **Not** a test. Not part of `:engine` public API. Not shipped in the jar
 * (this file lives in `src/test/kotlin`). Its only purpose is to serve
 * `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden`, which developers run **after an
 * intentional IR change** and commit alongside the change.
 *
 * **Never** edit `golden_ir.json` by hand:
 * 1. Hand-edits can miss fields or introduce typos that pass a diff-by-eye.
 * 2. The golden is compared **semantically** by `GoldenIrTest` — hand-edit
 *    that preserves semantics but changes formatting is fine, but a
 *    hand-edit that *changes* semantics is a bug, not a fix.
 *
 * **Workflow when you change the IR:**
 * 1. Change the IR (files in `:engine/.../ir/`).
 * 2. Run `./gradlew :engine:updateGolden`.
 * 3. `git diff engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json` — verify the diff
 *    is exactly what you expected. If it contains unexpected fields, you
 *    have an unintended IR change; investigate before committing.
 * 4. Commit the golden alongside the IR change.
 *
 * **Workflow when you do NOT change the IR:**
 * If `GoldenIrTest` fails and you did not touch `:engine/.../ir/`, one of:
 * - Someone else changed the IR (in this branch, via merge). Review their
 *   change, then run `updateGolden` if it is intentional.
 * - The parser changed (`JsonToIr`, `ConditionParser`). The golden
 *   captures parser output too, by design: a parser change that alters
 *   IR output is a breaking change for every adventure file.
 * - `test_adventure.json` changed. That is also a deliberate act; update
 *   the golden.
 */
private const val GOLDEN_PATH = "engine/src/test/resources/golden_ir.json"

private val PRETTY_JSON = Json {
    prettyPrint = true
    encodeDefaults = false
}

public fun main() {
    val classLoader = object {}.javaClass.classLoader
    val stream = classLoader.getResourceAsStream("test_adventure.json")
        ?: error(
            "test_adventure.json not found on classpath. " +
                    "The copy task in engine/build.gradle.kts should have placed it " +
                    "in engine/build/resources/test/. Make sure :engine:processTestResources ran.",
        )
    val rawJson = stream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }

    val result = JsonToIr.parse(rawJson)
    val adventure: Adventure = when (result) {
        is ParseResult.Success -> result.value
        is ParseResult.Failure -> {
            System.err.println("Cannot regenerate golden: test_adventure.json failed to parse.")
            result.errors.forEach { System.err.println("  ${it.message}") }
            kotlin.system.exitProcess(1)
        }
    }

    val text = PRETTY_JSON.encodeToString(Adventure.serializer(), adventure)
    val out = File(GOLDEN_PATH)
    out.parentFile.mkdirs()
    out.writeText(text)
    println("Wrote $GOLDEN_PATH (${text.length} chars, ${adventure.chapters.size} chapters)")
}
